# 關於 Think BIG

Think BIG（大想成業有限公司）是總部位於台灣、服務全球的企業 AI Agent 導入商。我們從守護企業資安出發，以 TB FRAME（我們的四階段導入方法：評估、建置、驗證、維運）把 AI Agent 建在公司自己的環境裡（公司設備，或公司名下的雲端主機），並提供一年陪跑維運。選地端版時，模型與文件都在公司設備內處理；選雲端輔助版時，問題與檢索到的文件段落會送到模型廠商處理。我們扮演企業的遠端 FDE（Forward Deployed Engineer，前沿部署工程師）團隊：從聽懂需求、建置知識庫與 AI Agent、上線，到後續維運，一手包辦；另有個人 AI 助理搭建方案。

地端部署不等於所有連線都在本機。若使用雲端模型或外部服務，相關請求仍會送出；需要資料不出公司時，須確認本機模型、外連限制與可用功能。

## 公司與服務範圍

Think BIG 的公司全名為大想成業有限公司，統一編號 62136066，總部位於台灣，服務範圍涵蓋全球。服務包含企業 AI Agent 導入、流程整合、資料與權限設計、情境驗收及年度治理與維運；另提供個人 AI 助理搭建與維護方案。

## 負責人與團隊

Think BIG 由負責人 NEO 領導。我們的工程團隊由多個建立在頂級模型之上的 AI Agent 組成，每一項交付在上線前都會經過資安審查。

AI Agent 負責建置、測試與維運的執行工作；範圍、核准與責任由人負責。

## 以 TB FRAME 管理交付

Assess 評估定義、Build 架構建置、Validate 驗證交付、Operate 治理維運，是導入方法的四個階段。TB READINESS（導入前自評，先確認流程、資料與準備條件）  提供初步自評；TB DELIVERY（依確認的範圍建置、測試並交付 AI 工作流程）  涵蓋導入建置；TB CONTINUITY（導入後一年的維護、問題追蹤與使用調整）  銜接年度治理與維運。企業服務依確認的範圍個別報價；三種方案於範圍凍結與資料到位後 30 天內交付。

[閱讀階段交付物與覆核責任](https://thinkbigtw.com/enterprise/process/)

## 治理原則

依最小權限配置資料與操作範圍。對外發送、花費及正式系統異動由指定負責人核准，變更留下原因、範圍、復原方式與驗證紀錄。

不公開客戶名稱、標誌、截圖或可推知身分的描述。能力說明以 Think BIG 團隊實際的運作與治理方式為依據，不代表第三方資安認證。

# About Think BIG | Think BIG

THINK BIG

# About Think BIG

Think BIG (Think BIG Make it Real CO., LTD.) is a Taiwan-based enterprise AI agent deployment company serving clients worldwide.

## Who we are

Think BIG (Think BIG Make it Real CO., LTD.) is an enterprise AI Agent deployment provider headquartered in Taiwan and serving clients worldwide. We start from keeping company data secure and build AI Agents inside the company's own environment (company equipment, or a cloud host registered to the company) with TB FRAME, our four-phase deployment method (assess, build, validate, operate), plus one year of hands-on maintenance. With the on-premises option, models and documents are processed on company equipment; with the cloud-assisted option, questions and retrieved document passages are sent to the model provider. We act as a remote FDE (Forward Deployed Engineer) team for the company: from understanding the need, building the knowledge base and AI Agents, and going live, to ongoing operations, handled end to end. Personal AI assistant setup plans are also available.

On-premises does not mean every connection stays on the machine.  If cloud models or external services are used, those requests still leave the device. When data must stay inside the company, local models, outbound restrictions and available features need to be confirmed first.

## Company and scope of service

# AI Agent Deployment Methodology | TB FRAME | Think BIG

TB FRAME METHODOLOGY

# Four phases.
Defined deliverables.
Verifiable results.

TB FRAME is Think BIG's structured approach to enterprise AI Agent deployment. Every phase produces a written record of deliverables, acceptance criteria and the conditions for hand-over — so you know exactly what was built and when it is ready to operate.

PHASE 1

## Assess

Define the scope and confirm that deployment is viable before writing a line of code.

Deliverables Workflow map of target processes; data inventory (sources, formats, access conditions); risk and dependency register; a proposed scope document signed off by both sides.

Acceptance criteria Client confirms the scope document accurately reflects the target workflows; data sources are accessible for integration scoping; no blocking dependency is unresolved.

Hand-over condition Written scope approval by the client's designated contact before any build work begins.

PHASE 2

## Build

Develop the AI Agents and integration layer against the agreed scope.

Deliverables Configured AI Agents; knowledge base or retrieval setup; integration connectors; operator guide; test scenario list prepared for Validate phase.

Acceptance criteria Agents respond to test scenarios within the agreed knowledge boundary; integration connectors return expected data; operator guide reviewed by client.

Hand-over condition Client confirms readiness for structured acceptance testing before Validate begins.

PHASE 3

## Validate

Run structured acceptance tests against agreed scenarios, document results and resolve gaps before go-live.

Deliverables Acceptance test results (pass/fail per scenario); gap resolution log; signed acceptance record; go-live checklist.

Acceptance criteria All agreed test scenarios pass or gaps are resolved and re-tested; client's designated contact signs the acceptance record.

Hand-over condition Signed acceptance record and completed go-live checklist before the system is opened to end users.

PHASE 4

## Operate

Support stable operations, monitor for anomalies and manage knowledge updates during the service period.

Deliverables Scheduled maintenance reports; anomaly and resolution log; knowledge base update records; scope-change requests (for items outside the original scope).

Acceptance criteria Maintenance reports are delivered within the agreed schedule; anomalies are responded to within the agreed SLA; scope-change items are logged and priced before work begins.

Hand-over condition Handover only occurs after a formal transition review when the service period ends or a new scope agreement is in place.

PLAN SCOPE AND TIMELINE

## See which plan includes which TB FRAME phases.

Plans range from a focused single-department deployment to a full multi-department rollout with annual operations. Each plan listing shows which phases are included, the number of AI Agents covered and the support period.

# How Enterprise AI Knowledge Bases Work | RAG Explained | Think BIG

ENTERPRISE KNOWLEDGE BASES

# How AI Agents answer questions from your own documents.

RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) enables AI Agents to answer questions from approved documents at retrieval time — no model training required. This article explains the key concepts, the data preparation process, permission controls and how acceptance testing verifies results.

## How RAG differs from general chat AI

General chat AI answers from patterns learned during training. When you ask a question it has not seen before — or one that depends on your internal documentation — it may generate a plausible-sounding but incorrect answer (hallucination).

RAG works differently. At query time the system retrieves the most relevant passages from your approved document set, then passes those passages together with the question to the AI model to compose a reply. The answer is grounded in your documents, not in the model's training data.

This matters for enterprise use: answers about your products, policies and processes must come from sources your business controls, not from whatever a general model has absorbed from the internet.

## RAG vs. fine-tuning: what to choose

Fine-tuning adjusts the weights of a model by training it on examples. It is expensive, requires labelled data, may expose your content to a model provider's training pipeline, and the model still risks hallucinating facts it has not seen. When your documents change, the model must be retrained.

RAG, by contrast, stores documents in a retrieval index you control. Update a document and the new content is immediately available at the next query. No retraining. No provider training risk (documents stay on your infrastructure). The source of every answer can be traced back to the retrieved passage.

For most enterprise knowledge-base applications — product documentation, policy Q&A, support SOP — RAG is the correct architecture.

## Data preparation

RAG quality depends heavily on data preparation. Documents that are inconsistent, out of date or poorly structured produce unreliable retrieval. The preparation steps we follow:

- Content audit.  Identify which documents are authoritative, which are drafts and which are superseded. Prioritise the authoritative set.

- Cleaning and formatting.  Remove formatting artefacts (headers repeated on every page, watermarks, page numbers that interrupt sentences) that confuse the retrieval index.

- Chunking strategy.  Decide how documents are split into retrievable segments. Chunk size and overlap affect recall — too large and irrelevant passages dilute the answer; too small and context is lost.

- Metadata tagging.  Tag each chunk with document source, version and category so retrieval can be filtered by permission or relevance scope.

- Embedding and indexing.  Convert text chunks into vector embeddings and store them in a retrieval index. The index is searchable by semantic similarity.

Data preparation is an ongoing activity. Documents are updated, rescinded and added. The maintenance plan defines how updates flow from source documents to the retrieval index.

## Privacy and permission controls

Not all documents should be available to all users. A customer-facing support agent should not retrieve from internal HR policy documents, and a finance agent should not expose board-level materials to a general assistant.

Permission controls are implemented at the retrieval layer — each query is filtered against the user's permission scope before retrieval results are assembled. At deployment we define:

- Which document collections each AI Agent may retrieve from

- Which user roles or channels may query which agents

- Whether any collections are excluded from external channels entirely

For on-premises deployments, documents and the retrieval index remain within your infrastructure. The AI model processes only the retrieved passages relevant to the query — it does not have persistent access to the full document set.

## Acceptance testing for knowledge bases

Building a knowledge base without a formal acceptance test is building without verification. Our acceptance process uses a prepared scenario set that includes:

- In-scope questions  — questions the system should answer correctly from the indexed documents

- Boundary questions  — questions at the edge of the indexed scope; the system should indicate when it cannot find a source rather than guessing

- Out-of-scope questions  — questions outside the indexed scope; the system must decline clearly

Results are logged per scenario (pass/fail, source passage retrieved, response quality) and reviewed with the client. Gaps are fixed and re-tested before go-live sign-off.

## Common failure modes

Retrieval misses The correct passage exists but is not retrieved. Usually caused by poor chunking, inconsistent terminology between documents and queries, or an inadequate embedding model for the domain language.

Incorrect citation The retrieved passage is plausible but from a superseded or draft version. Prevented by strict content audit and version tagging in the metadata layer.

Over-retrieval Too many passages are retrieved; the model averages across them and produces a vague answer. Prevented by tightening the retrieval filter and reducing chunk overlap.

Confident hallucination The model fills in details not in the retrieved passage. Monitored through acceptance testing and by reviewing system prompt guardrails that require citation of source text.

Stale knowledge base Source documents are updated but the index is not. Prevented by the maintenance plan, which specifies a review cycle and an update trigger whenever source documents change.

## Think BIG's approach

We deploy RAG using on-premises or private-cloud vector stores that remain within your infrastructure. No document content is sent to a public indexing service. The retrieval index is owned by you and can be migrated or audited at any time.

Our scope documents specify the document collections to be indexed, the chunking and metadata strategy, the permission filters per agent and channel, and the acceptance scenario set before build begins. This means you can verify what was agreed and what was delivered.

# AI Agent Acceptance Framework: Deliverables, Exceptions & Approvals | Think BIG

ENTERPRISE INSIGHTS

# AI Agent Acceptance Framework: Deliverables, Exceptions and Approvals

Use input conditions, deliverable specifications, exception handling, and approval mechanisms to build an acceptance framework — and carry verification records into ongoing change management.

IN THIS ARTICLE

## Convert Business Goals into Acceptance Conditions

Translate work objectives into verifiable deliverable specifications: output format, required fields, data sources, and review roles. For example, reply drafts should include cited references; summary tables should list missing data. Replace broad benefit statements with checkable conditions.

## Cover Normal, Anomalous, and Unauthorized Scenarios

Prepare scenarios for complete data, unverifiable data, missing fields, service interruptions, and insufficient permissions. Verify that the AI reports accurately, stops unauthorized operations, and routes issues to the designated handler per the agreed procedure.

## Build Traceable Test Evidence

Record test conditions, configurations, input ranges, expected results, and actual results so acceptance conclusions can be re-traced. Retention and access rules for sensitive data must be agreed separately — test records should not arbitrarily copy complete raw data.

## Include Human Approval in the Acceptance Scope

Human-in-the-loop requires verifiable control points. For steps that require approval, confirm the system stops execution before authorization is granted. Technical automation capability does not equal business authorization.

## Perform Impact Validation on Every Change

Model, data, and permission adjustments can all affect outputs. Per the governance-operations phase of TB FRAME (our four-stage deployment method: Assess, Build, Validate, Operate) , register the change scope, impact, and rollback method before re-validating with relevant scenarios, extending acceptance into ongoing operations.

# Will New AI Agents Replace the Lobster (OpenClaw)?

Think BIG Editorial

Grok, Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and others are launching fast. This guide covers what AI Agents are available in 2026, how each charges for usage, what to do when quotas run out, and where OpenClaw fits for long-running tasks.

Last updated: 2026-10-02 | Data verified: 2026-09-30

New AI Agents will not make OpenClaw (the Lobster) obsolete — they are designed for different purposes. Each one is excellent. But for long-running tasks where cost control matters, brand AI Agents are not the first choice, though they are great for collaboration.

- Brand AI Agents tie costs to subscription quotas. They suit collaboration tasks within brand ecosystems (Gmail, Teams, WhatsApp).

- Open-source AI Agents (like OpenClaw, Hermes) let you choose your own model and pay per actual usage — suitable for 24/7 operations with predictable costs.

- The two types work well together: run OpenClaw for long-running routine tasks; use brand AI Agents for collaboration or ecosystem-specific work.

## Key Takeaway

Each one is excellent. But for long-running tasks where cost control matters, brand AI Agents are not the first choice — though they are great for collaboration.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Will new AI Agents replace OpenClaw (the Lobster)?

The two serve different purposes and work well together. Common brand AI Agents in 2026 include Grok Bot (xAI), Claude (Anthropic), ChatGPT Agent and dots (OpenAI), Gemini Spark (Google), Muse (Meta), Copilot Autopilot (Microsoft), and Manus. Each one is excellent, but for long-running tasks where cost control matters, brand AI Agents are not the first choice — though they are great for collaboration. OpenClaw and Hermes, as open-source AI Agents, let you choose your own model, pay per actual usage, and run 24/7.

Q: What AI Agents are available in 2026?

Two main types: (1) Brand AI Agents — subscription-based with usage quotas, such as Claude, ChatGPT Agent, Gemini Spark, Grok Bot, Muse, Copilot Autopilot, Manus. (2) Open-source AI Agents — software is free, you pay per model usage, such as OpenClaw (Lobster) and Hermes Agent.

Q: What should I do when my AI subscription quota runs out?

Common options: wait for quota reset, upgrade your plan, purchase additional credits, or route long-running background work to an open-source AI Agent (like OpenClaw) that charges per actual usage.

Q: Can brand AI Agents and OpenClaw be used together?

Yes. A common setup: OpenClaw handles 24/7 routine tasks; brand AI Agents handle collaboration tasks or ecosystem-specific work. → [OpenClaw + coding agent](https://thinkbigtw.com/full-agent/) / [Dual AI Agent plan](https://thinkbigtw.com/dual-agent/)

Q: Does Think BIG's pricing include AI model fees?

No. Think BIG's service fee covers installation and setup only. Third-party AI model usage fees are calculated based on your actual usage and paid directly to the model provider. See [FAQ](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/faq/).

# Evaluating an AI Implementation Partner: Capability, Delivery & Governance | Think BIG

ENTERPRISE INSIGHTS

# Evaluating an AI Implementation Partner: Capability, Delivery and Governance

Use process fit, data governance, acceptance testing, and ongoing operations as four dimensions to evaluate whether an AI deployment service has clear execution and accountability scope.

IN THIS ARTICLE

## Define Technical Requirements Through Business Processes

Evaluate deployment capability through actual business workflows: where data comes from, which steps the AI handles, who receives the deliverables, and who is responsible for review. Models and demo interfaces can illustrate tool capability, but procurement evaluation must also cover process integration and execution accountability.

## Confirm Service Boundaries Through Deliverables

Request an explicit list of process diagrams, data inventories, permission configurations, test records, and operating procedures — along with acceptance conditions for each item. Evaluating clearly scoped work makes it easier to compare the accountability and inclusions of different deployment services.

## Trace Data Governance to Transmitted Fields

Confirm the deployment environment, external model, log and backup locations, access roles, and transmitted fields item by item. On-premises configurations still require evaluation of external integrations. Data governance cannot be determined by host location alone.

## Confirm Exception Handling and Human Handoff

Include missing data, unverifiable responses, service interruptions, and unauthorized operations in the acceptance scope. Confirm how the system stops, reports, and routes issues to a human handler, and designate a responsible person with decision authority.

## Establish Clear Maintenance and Exit Responsibilities

Confirm service fees, equipment, model usage costs, and third-party services item by item, then define issue reporting, change approval, configuration handover, and service termination procedures. ROI assessment should be based on the company's own process baseline and actual costs — not generic multipliers.

## Think BIG's Delivery and Governance Basis

Think BIG organizes assessment, build, validation, and operations through TB FRAME (our four-stage deployment method: Assess, Build, Validate, Operate) , with a year of continuity support through TB CONTINUITY (one year of maintenance, issue tracking, and usage adjustments after deployment) . Capability statements are grounded in actual change logs, daily check runs, and evidence verification. Client identities, data, and screenshots are not used as external marketing material.

# AI Implementation Glossary | Think BIG

THINK BIG

# AI Implementation Glossary

From on-premises deployment and data sovereignty to scenario acceptance — consistent definitions for evaluating AI Agent deployment scope.

This glossary is organized around our deployment process, governance documentation, and personal plans — use it to align terms when evaluating services.

Further reading: [TB FRAME (our four-stage deployment method: Assess, Build, Validate, Operate)  deployment process](https://thinkbigtw.com/enterprise/process/), [data governance](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/), [acceptance framework](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/guides/ai-acceptance/), [personal plans](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/pricing/).

## AI and Collaboration

### AI Agent

An AI assistant that executes workflows within approved data, tools, and operational scope; deliverables and significant actions still require review by a designated person.

In a Think BIG deployment, work is defined by approved knowledge, expected deliverables, and prohibited operations.

### Agentic AI

The practice of using AI Agents to execute processes, use tools, and produce reviewable outcomes.

In a Think BIG deployment, we first confirm data, tools, and human decision boundaries before evaluating suitable workflows.

### Human-in-the-loop

Having AI support work products and process execution under designated human approval and review control points.

In a Think BIG deployment, outbound sending, spending, and formal system changes require approval from a designated person.

## Deployment and Delivery

### TB FRAME

Think BIG's AI Agent deployment methodology, divided into four phases: Assess, Build, Validate, Operate.

In a Think BIG deployment, each phase has defined deliverables and review responsibilities.

### TB READINESS (pre-deployment self-assessment: confirm process, data, and readiness conditions)

A six-question deployment readiness self-assessment. Answers are computed only in the browser — nothing is transmitted or stored. Results do not constitute certification or a formal consulting evaluation.

On the Think BIG website, you can use the self-assessment to organize pre-deployment prerequisites before confirming details with a consultant.

### TB DELIVERY (build, test, and deliver AI workflows per confirmed scope)

An AI Agent deployment build service covering process inventory, data and permission design, AI Agent configuration, acceptance testing, and operational handover.

In a Think BIG deployment, build scope and acceptance responsibilities are confirmed before work begins.

### TB CONTINUITY (one year of maintenance, issue tracking, and usage adjustments after deployment)

An annual AI Agent governance and operations service providing one year of continuity, issue tracking, maintenance checks, and change records within the agreed scope.

In a Think BIG deployment, the service contact, maintenance scope, and expansion handling are written into the agreement.

### Scenario Acceptance

Verifying deliverable specifications, exception handling, and human approval mechanisms using normal, missing-data, service-interruption, and unauthorized scenarios.

In a Think BIG deployment, test records and outcomes are reviewed by a designated person.

## Data and Governance

### On-Premises Deployment

Deploying work data and execution environments on company-designated equipment. If external models or services are used, transmitted fields and authorizations must still be confirmed.

In a Think BIG deployment, equipment, models, and external connection scope are all confirmed together.

### Data Sovereignty

The company confirms data sources, processing locations, access roles, and external transmission scope, while retaining authorization and decision-making responsibility.

In a Think BIG deployment, the data and permissions inventory must be traceable with clearly listed approval responsibilities.

### Least Privilege

Opening data and operational scope only as required by the work, confirmed by a designated person.

In a Think BIG deployment, the fact that a tool is capable of an operation does not mean it is authorized by default.

### Human Approval

Critical operations such as outbound sending, spending, and formal system changes are decided by a designated person before execution.

In a Think BIG deployment, acceptance also includes verifying that operations stop when not approved.

### Auditability

Retaining source, operation, and verification records so that processes and conclusions can be re-traced.

In a Think BIG deployment, accountability is confirmed through data and permissions inventories, change records, and acceptance records.

### Change Log

Before adjusting configurations or processes, record the reason, scope, responsible person, and rollback method.

In a Think BIG deployment, changes require prior approval, then validation with relevant scenarios to confirm impact.

## Tools and Usage Costs

### MCP

Model Context Protocol — an open protocol for connecting AI tools to data and functions. The actual accessible scope is still determined by account permissions and configuration.

In Think BIG services, MCP integrations still require verification of tools, accounts, and actual permissions.

### Model Usage Fee

The cost paid to a model provider based on AI model usage. The local personal plan does not incur this separately; cloud-based usage is billed per use and is not included in the service fee.

In Think BIG personal services, the local plan does not incur model usage fees. When using cloud-based large models, usage fees are paid directly to the model provider based on actual use.

### Zero-Token Priority

Preferring fixed rules or code — which require no model inference — to handle suitable tasks.

This design principle is used in the Think BIG personal skill package. The local plan incurs no model usage fees; cloud-based usage may still generate model usage fees depending on use.

### RAG

Retrieval-Augmented Generation: first retrieving relevant knowledge, then providing it to the model as the basis for its response.

When evaluating enterprise knowledge Q&A, Think BIG first confirms data sources, authorization, and answer traceability. The actual architecture is confirmed per requirements. [Learn more about RAG data preparation and acceptance](https://thinkbigtw.com/enterprise/rag/).

### Skill

Instructions and tool configurations that enable an AI Agent to execute specific tasks.

In Think BIG personal services, skill items and scope are confirmed based on the selected plan and an interview.

### OpenClaw

An AI Agent platform that can be configured with skills and tools in a designated environment.

Think BIG personal starter services offer an OpenClaw installation option. Equipment and account requirements must be confirmed first.

### Hermes Agent

An AI Agent tool for configuring AI assistants and workflows.

Think BIG personal plans offer Hermes installation and configuration options. Feature scope is confirmed per the corresponding plan page.

# Hermes vs OpenClaw: Which Personal AI Agent Should You Choose?

Think BIG Editorial

What actually separates OpenClaw from Hermes Agent? For one person, one company, different work scenarios — which should you choose? Plain-English breakdown of both tools' positioning, memory models, skill ecosystems, and who each suits best — plus a plan chart showing which Think BIG personal plan includes which tool.

Published: 2026-09-13

Both OpenClaw and Hermes Agent are AI assistants you can install on your own computer. Hermes Agent is open-sourced by Nous Research and is one of the products Think BIG provides installation services for. When choosing, start by confirming your workflow and what features you need.

- OpenClaw is an assistant installed on your computer that gets things done  — checking messages, organizing files, running fixed workflows, connecting the tools you already use.

- Hermes Agent supports cross-conversation memory and self-learning, turning task experience into skills; it can be installed standalone or chained with OpenClaw for a split-role setup.

The following organizes use cases, support scope, and pricing by personal installation plan.

## One-sentence summary: what's the difference

OpenClaw is like an assistant who can run errands for you; Hermes Agent is like an assistant who organizes information and thinks things through for you . One is action-oriented, the other is thought-oriented. Both run on your computer and help you do work — just different kinds of work. You can install both if you want; it depends on what your work looks like.

## Four angles of comparison

### 1. Positioning: getting things done vs. thinking things through

OpenClaw excels at "you give it an action and it runs it and shows you the result": fixed workflows, scheduled reminders, replying to messages, organizing files, connecting tools. You give it commands more than you chat with it.

Hermes excels at "you want to clarify something and it helps you work it out": long conversations, document rewriting, research synthesis, drafting, problem solving. You'll have more back-and-forth dialogue with it; its value shows in how fast you produce written work.

### 2. Memory model: action context vs. conversation context

OpenClaw's memory leans toward "what this task did": task and state continuity, remembering results when each task ends for next time's reference.

Hermes's memory leans toward "what we've discussed and what conclusions we reached": cross-conversation, cross-topic accumulation — more like a notebook and thought thread.

### 3. Skill ecosystem: workflow skills vs. document and knowledge skills

OpenClaw's skills are built around "letting it take action": communication (messaging platforms), files, scheduling, browser, custom scripts.

Hermes's skills are built around "letting it think more deeply and write faster": long-document summarization, research synthesis, knowledge-base comparison, writing-style adaptation.

### 4. Suitable scenarios: one person's daily life vs. multi-person collaboration

OpenClaw is best suited for a single person who wants to automate daily chores.

Hermes is especially useful for solo operators, people who write a lot every day (proposals, documents, emails), or those who want to have ongoing dialogue with their work content.

## How to choose? Ask yourself three questions

- Do you more often "tell AI to do something" or "discuss things with AI"?  Former: OpenClaw. Latter: Hermes.

- Is your work mostly chores, or mostly writing?  Lots of chores: OpenClaw. Lots of writing: Hermes.

- Do you want one or two assistants working separately?  One: start with the Persona edition. Two but independent: Co-existence edition. Two with memory sync and collaboration: Dual AI Agent (with collaboration room).

If you're unsure: install OpenClaw first and run it for a week or two. You'll learn what you're still missing. Then decide whether to add Hermes. Most people start with OpenClaw.

## FAQ

Q: What is the relationship between OpenClaw and Hermes?

OpenClaw is a local AI assistant that runs on your computer and executes tasks; Hermes Agent is an open-source self-learning AI assistant from Nous Research. You can install either one independently or chain them together as a dual-assistant setup. Which to start with depends on your workflow.

Q: Is one enough, or should I install both?

If you have one person and one clear use case, one is enough. If you want two assistants with different styles dividing work, or want to separate workflow execution from daily messaging, install both.

Q: Does having both installed cost a lot?

If you want two assistants running independently without shared memory, choose the Co-existence edition. If you want shared memory and a collaboration room, choose the Dual AI Agent (with cross-Agent collaboration room, 2-hour online tech walkthrough + 7-day post-installation support).

Q: Is the Hermes on Think BIG the same as Hermes Agent online?

Yes. Hermes Agent is an open-source self-learning AI assistant from Nous Research. Think BIG's service assists with installation, configuration, and guidance on your computer.

Q: Can I maintain both on an annual plan?

Yes. Annual Flagship is the plan for both assistants with shared memory plus full-year maintenance. Premium Annual is the single-system annual plan. Decide how many assistants you want before looking at annual plans — it'll save you a roundabout route.

# On-Premises AI and Data Sovereignty: From Deployment Location to Data Governance | Think BIG

ENTERPRISE INSIGHTS

# On-Premises AI and Data Sovereignty: From Deployment Location to Data Governance

From deployment location to external services, access permissions, logs, and exit handover — clarify the actual control scope of data sovereignty.

IN THIS ARTICLE

## Evaluate Deployment Location and External Integrations Separately

A fully on-premises configuration lets models and designated data run on company equipment. If your workflow connects to external models, communication services, or other integrations, you still need to confirm what is actually transmitted, the account terms, and the purpose. Deployment location and data flow are separate evaluation items.

## Build a Complete Data Flow Inventory

List data sources, AI processing environments, output recipients, logs, and backups — annotating purpose, access roles, retention method, and external services at each stage. The data flow inventory serves as the shared basis for permission configuration and future change evaluation.

## Distinguish Model Training from Service Data Use Terms

How a vendor uses your input data depends on the specific product, account, and contract settings. Before deploying, separately confirm the service processing terms, retention policies, and model training use — avoid inferring individual plan conditions from the vendor's general brand statements.

## Configure Access Scope Using the Least-Privilege Principle

Grant only the data and operational permissions required by the work. Outbound sending, spending, and formal system changes should require approval from a designated person. Any permission additions or adjustments must leave a change record.

## Plan Data and Configuration Exit Handover

Define in advance the custodianship responsibilities for accounts, configurations, data, and records, as well as the transfer, retention, and deletion procedures when the service ends. Data ownership and ongoing use conditions should be included in the agreed service scope.

# OpenClaw Installation Explained: What the Persona Edition Actually Sets Up

Think BIG Editorial

Stuck on the OpenClaw install? This guide breaks down the installation service clearly: what the Persona Edition sets up, how to choose between the supportive or challenging personality, what the installation process looks like, and how pricing works. Read it and you'll know whether it's worth it for you.

Updated: 2026-08-31

You probably arrived here like this: you saw someone using an AI assistant like OpenClaw to offload their repetitive daily tasks — and it looked effortless. Then you opened a tutorial, got stuck on step one — terminal, environment variables, a wall of commands you didn't understand. Three minutes later you closed the tab, thinking "forget it, I'm not an engineer."

This guide is here to explain it plainly. What does the OpenClaw installation service  actually do — what does the service fee cover (including personality selection!) — and what do you still need to handle yourself. After reading, you can judge for yourself: is this worth paying for?

We're not here to sell you anxiety, and we won't tell you "you'll fall behind if you don't do this." It's just a tool — only use it if it's worth using.

## What is OpenClaw? What is "OpenClaw installation"?

OpenClaw is an AI Agent framework that runs on your own computer. Unlike regular chatbots, it doesn't just reply to you — it can actually "take action": organizing files, replying to messages, running fixed workflows, connecting to tools you use.

That sounds great, but the problem is installation . Getting it running involves a setup process that isn't very user-friendly for non-engineers: the environment needs to be right, permissions need to be opened, various services need to be connected. Get one step wrong and it won't run — and the error messages are in English.

That's why the OpenClaw installation service  exists: you don't need to touch those commands. Engineers connect remotely and set everything up, get it running, verify it works — you just watch. AI assistant installation  was never meant to be something you wrestle with alone.

## What does the Persona Edition set up? Item by item

This is what everyone wants to know. Here's the Persona Edition broken down so you can see each piece:

### 1. Official OpenClaw, one Agent

What's installed is the official OpenClaw release — not a modified or counterfeit version. "One Agent" means you have one dedicated AI assistant instance running on your own machine.

### 2. Local deployment — data stays on your computer

The Persona Edition AI Assistant is installed on your own computer, not sent to some cloud somewhere. For many people, "my stuff is in my own hands" is itself valuable.

### 3. Remote installation by Taiwan-based engineers

Taiwan-based engineers connect remotely via AnyDesk or DeskIn to do the installation. Full communication in English is available. You can see everything the engineer does. The installation is complete only when it's running and verified working.

### 4. Full personal skill package + personality selection + Coding Agent

The Persona Edition includes a full personal skill package + 1 custom helper, tailored more closely to your work scenarios than a bare-bones install. You can also choose a supportive  (warm, affirming without being sycophantic) or challenging  (direct and sharp, without personal attacks) personality, plus 1–2 Coding Agent connections.

One-sentence summary:  The service fee covers an OpenClaw AI assistant that's installed, running, with the personality you chose, on your own computer — plus the service of Taiwan-based engineers installing it remotely until it works. It is not a tutorial document for you to follow yourself.

## What does the installation process look like? Your part is actually minimal

Many people think the installation process is complicated, but your part is light:

- Place order:  Complete your Persona Edition order.

- Schedule a time:  The engineer contacts you based on the order and arranges a mutually convenient installation slot.

- Remote connection:  At the scheduled time, the engineer connects to your computer via AnyDesk/DeskIn.

- Have a coffee and watch:  This part is almost entirely the engineer operating. You just need to be nearby — when they need you to confirm an account or authorize something, you click.

- Verify it works:  When done, together you confirm the AI assistant can run and respond before the session ends.

Really — your workload is roughly "turn on computer, allow remote access, watch." That's the point of the installation service: leave the hard parts to the people who know how.

## Honest section: what do you still need to prepare?

This section we always state clearly, because finding out "there were other things to handle" after installation is a bad feeling. Here's what the Persona Edition doesn't include and what you need to have ready:

- Equipment check:  Before installation, please take a screenshot and send to the engineer (Mac: check if RAM is 16 GB or more, whether you have an Apple M chip; Windows: check NVIDIA GPU and whether GPU memory is 8 GB or more). If specs qualify, a local model is installed; if not, a cloud-based large model is used instead — same plan, same price.

- Cloud version only — API Key:  When switching to a cloud-based large model, you need to register for that model's account (API Key) yourself. The engineer will guide you through it but won't do it on your behalf.

- Cloud version model usage fees:  When using cloud-based large models, the AI model is billed per use — you pay that directly based on actual usage. It's not included in the service fee. Local version: no model usage fees.

- Messaging integrations require official accounts:  If you want to connect the AI assistant to a messaging platform, only official accounts with Messaging API access are supported — personal accounts cannot be connected. Official accounts can typically be registered for free; the engineer will guide you through it.

- Some third-party services require free registration:  Certain advanced integrations use third-party services (such as free database services) that require you to register a free account yourself.

We'd rather tell you upfront than have you feel ambushed later. Service fee is a one-time payment. Local version: no additional model fees. Cloud version model usage fees are separate.  Those two sentences are the entire fee structure.

## What can you do with it once it's set up?

Installation is just the starting point. The Persona Edition gives you an AI assistant that can take action. What you actually use it for depends on your work — common examples:

- Hand off daily repetitive, mindless but time-consuming tasks.

- Have it follow the workflows you set up and do fixed things at fixed times.

- Speak to it in plain language and it moves things forward — rather than giving you a wall of information you still have to process yourself.

To make it understand your work better and know more "moves," you add skill packages. The Persona Edition already includes the full personal skill package + 1 custom helper; additional packs can be added later.

## Want to upgrade? What comes after the Persona Edition

The Persona Edition AI Assistant is the first tier of personal plans, intentionally made easy to get started. After using it, you can scale up as needed:

- Skill package add-ons:  Want more skills? Add-on skill packages are available in three tiers: 10, 20, or 40 packs (priced on request). These follow a "minimal model calls" design philosophy so each call is more cost-efficient.

- Multi-Agent collaboration:  If you need multiple AI assistants dividing work and connecting more tools, there are more comprehensive plans available. These are custom-scoped — we discuss your needs first, then quote.

No need to get everything at once. Get the Persona Edition running first, find out what you actually need, then add. That's the clearest way to spend your money.

## What if you decide you don't want it anymore?

Worth mentioning. If you later no longer want OpenClaw, there's a corresponding uninstall service (priced on request) where the engineer remotely removes everything cleanly — no residual files left on your computer. Using it comfortably is your right; having it cleaned up properly when you're done is our responsibility.

## FAQ

Q: I have no programming knowledge. Can I still get OpenClaw installed?

Yes. That's exactly why the installation service exists. The engineer does the entire installation remotely via AnyDesk/DeskIn. You just turn on your computer, allow the connection, and watch. When authorization is needed, you click.

Q: How much does the OpenClaw installation cost?

The Persona Edition AI Assistant service fee is priced on request, one-time payment, including supportive or challenging personality selection, full personal skill package + 1 custom helper + Coding Agent connection. Important note: the AI model API usage fee is billed separately based on your actual usage — you pay that directly. Local version: no model usage fees. These are two separate costs; we'll explain them clearly upfront.

Q: What's the difference between the Persona Edition and higher-tier plans?

The Persona Edition is a full personal skill package + personality selection + Coding Agent connection, single AI Agent locally deployed, no ongoing maintenance. Higher plans include: Dual AI Agent Co-existence Edition (two running independently, no memory sync), Dual AI Agent (with memory sync and collaboration room), or annual plans (a full year of engineer support). Simply put: Persona Edition is "get it installed with personality and running"; higher tiers are "run more complexity, with someone maintaining it long-term."

Q: Will my data get uploaded to the cloud?

The Persona Edition is locally deployed — the AI assistant runs on your own computer. Which AI model it connects to and how data flows depends on your model choice and configuration. This will be explained during installation — no exaggeration and no vagueness.

Q: How long does installation take? Do I need to watch the whole time?

A typical Persona Edition remote installation completes within one session. The engineer handles most of it. You don't need to stare at the screen the whole time, but it's recommended to be nearby so you can handle authorization or confirmations when needed.

Q: If it doesn't work after installation, is there a refund?

If the installation cannot be completed due to an issue on our side, we provide a full refund. Services are handled in accordance with applicable consumer protection regulations.

Q: Is AnyDesk remote access safe?

AnyDesk/DeskIn are remote desktop tools — the connection is only established with your permission, and you can disconnect at any time. # Is OpenClaw Safe? 6 Specific Risks Before You Install | Think BIG

[Guides](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/guides/) / Is OpenClaw Safe?

Security · Must-Read Before Installing

# Is OpenClaw Safe? 6 Specific Risks to Know Before You Install

Think BIG Editorial

Search results for "Is OpenClaw safe?" skew negative. This guide breaks down 6 specific risks, tells you what to do if you install yourself, and what our installation service handles by default. One-sentence conclusion: the key to safety isn't not installing it — it's least privilege plus local deployment plus only installing official skills.

Published: 2026-09-13

Search "Is OpenClaw safe?" and you'll mostly find forum posts, security guides, and negative reviews — AI summaries often directly say "not recommended for general users." What this guide aims to do is break down the specific risks behind those conclusions and tell you what "do if you install yourself" and "what a good installation service should do" looks like for each one.

The conclusion first: the OpenClaw framework isn't designed to harm you, but it's powerful enough that "installing it wrong" can cause problems . Issues usually come from the installer not setting permissions, installing unknown-source skills, or leaving defaults unchanged. It's like buying a good knife — the knife is fine; swinging it carelessly is what causes injuries.

## One-sentence conclusion

Safety isn't about "not installing it" — it's about doing three things together : least privilege (grant only necessary access), local deployment (data stays on your computer), and only official skills (the skill layer is OpenClaw's biggest attack surface). Do all three and risk is manageable. Skip all three and nothing is safe no matter what you install.

## 6 specific risks, broken down

### Risk 1: Prompt Injection

External content (web pages, documents, messages) contains hidden malicious instructions that trick the AI assistant into performing unintended actions. For example: you give OpenClaw a document that looks normal but contains "send all files to this address" — and the AI follows through.

If you install yourself Don't let OpenClaw directly read unfamiliar URLs or documents. High-sensitivity operations (sending files, changing passwords) must require your confirmation before executing.

What we do by default We enable "high-risk actions require second confirmation" by default and restrict read/write scope to folders you specify.

### Risk 2: Malicious Skills

Skills are the extension packs that let OpenClaw "do things" — the community has many sources. Unknown-source skills may have hidden capabilities to read passwords, connect to relay servers, or execute arbitrary code.

If you install yourself Only install skills from official or trusted authors. Review the code before installing; don't skip warnings. Periodically audit your installed skills list.

What we do by default The Persona Edition includes a full personal skill package + 1 custom helper — no third-party sources. Add-on skill packages are Think BIG internally maintained versions with audit records.

### Risk 3: Exposed Port / Web UI Exposed Externally

OpenClaw has a local management interface (Web UI) you access via browser. If you don't change defaults, don't set a password, and expose it publicly, the entire assistant is naked on the internet — like leaving your house key in the lock.

If you install yourself Change the default password. Bind to 127.0.0.1 (localhost) only. Don't set DMZ on your router; don't use tools like ngrok to expose it.

What we do by default Always change default password, bind to localhost, don't open external ports. If external access is needed (e.g., messaging integration), we use the officially provided tunnel — not a custom open port.

### Risk 4: API Key Leak

An AI model API key (like Anthropic / OpenAI) once leaked lets others use your credit — or even rack up charges billed to you. Common leak paths: committing it to a public GitHub repo, posting it in social media screenshots, or handing it directly to someone else.

If you install yourself Store keys in local environment variables — never commit them. Don't push .env files to public repos. Regularly check usage in the model provider's dashboard.

What we do by default Local version: no API key needed. Cloud version: you apply for and keep your own key. The engineer only guides the process, doesn't apply on your behalf and doesn't retain your key. Deleted from connection cache in front of you after installation.

### Risk 5: Accidental Deletion or Overwrite

OpenClaw takes action — and "taking action" includes deleting files, editing files, sending emails, sending messages. Without protection, the AI might misread a situation and delete an entire folder, or send a draft message to someone it shouldn't.

If you install yourself Set second confirmation for high-risk actions (deleting files, sending external messages). Keep a change log. Back up important data before granting permissions.

What we do by default Default: writable scope restricted to folders you specify. External message sending requires phone push notification confirmation. 90-day change record kept.

### Risk 6: Outdated Version / Unpatched Vulnerabilities

Every software has vulnerabilities — OpenClaw included. Install it and don't update, and six months later you may hit a vulnerability that's been patched but you haven't applied.

If you install yourself Subscribe to official update announcements. Manually update every 1–3 months.

What we do by default Persona Edition: installed until it runs — you decide when to update. Premium Annual and Annual Flagship include weekly maintenance; we handle updates.

## Comparison: self-install vs. professional installation

The real value of professional installation isn't "installing it for you" — it's getting all these defaults right the first time.  The six items below are what we handle by default during installation; if you install yourself, you need to do each of these manually.

Item Self-install effort Professional install default
Change default password Find config file, change, restart Already changed at completion

Bind localhost, no external exposure Check default binding IP Default 127.0.0.1

Second confirmation for high-risk actions Modify policy settings Enabled by default

Skills whitelist Maintain list yourself Official only

API key security Local version: no key needed. Cloud: set env variables yourself, don't commit Local version: no key needed. Cloud: guide you to apply yourself; engineer doesn't retain it

Updates and maintenance Every 1–3 months manually Annual plans include weekly maintenance

## Who should install it? Who shouldn't?

### Suitable candidates

- Regular workers who want to automate repetitive tasks and are willing to spend an hour on basic configuration.

- Solo operators who want multiple AI assistants dividing up daily workload.

- People mentally prepared for "you install it, you maintain it" — and don't want to be held hostage by their tools.

### Who we'd advise against installing it

- Work computers or company-issued equipment: IT policy usually doesn't permit this kind of tool in a corporate environment. Check with your IT department first.

- People completely unwilling to learn basic configuration (even changing passwords): even with professional installation, you need to learn to check logs and change passwords.

- People expecting "install and everything defaults to working, zero maintenance": any tool that can take action carries configuration responsibility — you can't outsource that to the tool itself.

## If you decide to install it, do these three defaults first

- Change the default password  — not doing this is like not locking the door.

- Bind to localhost  — don't expose the Web UI externally.

- Only install official skills  — don't touch unknown community skill packages.

Doing these three things substantially reduces risks from permissions, skill sources, and access configuration. The remaining risks come from genuinely targeted attacks — which still require ongoing monitoring, updates, and anomaly handling.

## Why this article exists on Think BIG's website

Because search results on this topic are almost entirely negative — forums, security guides, media coverage, and no commercial service page at all. We're a team that provides OpenClaw installation services and deals with these risks every day  — how to set permissions, how to explain risks to clients, how to make it actually usable after installation without hitting landmines. We have first-hand experience.

This article isn't here to tell you to "go ahead and install it without worry." It's to help you see the risks clearly, understand how to handle them, and then make your own decision .

## FAQ

Q: Is OpenClaw safe?

It depends on how you install it. Most security risks come from "no permissions set after installation," "unknown-source skills installed," or "default account not password-changed" — not from the framework itself being unsafe. Least privilege, local deployment, and only installing official skills are the three basic things.

Q: Will OpenClaw steal my data?

OpenClaw in local deployment runs on your own computer and doesn't actively upload any data anywhere by default. Data leaves through only two paths: calling an external AI model API (necessary for cloud version; local version processes on your machine — questions don't go to the model provider; messages via messaging platforms do pass through that platform), and external services you connect to. If you haven't connected those, OpenClaw only runs on your computer.

Q: Can OpenClaw be hacked?

The framework is actively updated with patches for known vulnerabilities. But if you've opened external ports with default passwords, or installed unknown-source skills, the hacking risk is real. We always change default passwords, don't open external ports, and restrict skill sources during installation.

Q: Couldn't the engineer tamper with things during remote installation?

We use AnyDesk/DeskIn for the remote session — you can see everything the engineer does throughout. We won't ask you for any account passwords. Keys and passwords are never transmitted via chat. After the session ends, no remote access is retained.

Q: Who should not install OpenClaw?

Three types of people: (1) work computers or company-issued equipment — IT policy usually disallows this kind of tool; (2) people completely unwilling to spend any time learning basic configuration; (3) people who expect "install and everything runs on defaults, zero maintenance."

Q: How often do I need to update after installation?

The OpenClaw framework typically releases an official update every 1–3 months. After installation we recommend subscribing to official announcements. Annual plans (Premium Annual, Annual Flagship) include weekly maintenance and 48-hour failure repair — we handle updates. The Persona Edition is installed once to run; you decide when to update.

## Conclusion

Whether OpenClaw is safe depends on whether you got the basic configuration right during installation . Common risks come from basic mistakes like "no permissions set," "unknown-source skills installed," "default password unchanged" — these are avoidable with an extra hour of setup.

If you're willing to spend that hour, or willing to have engineers do it right the first time (including personality selection), OpenClaw is a tool that can save you significant time every day. If you're completely unwilling to learn or have someone set it up — no tool like this will suit you, not just OpenClaw.

Think it through before installing. After installation, change the password, bind to localhost, install only official skills. With those three things done, risk is manageable.

### Decided to install it? Start with the Persona Edition

Taiwan-based engineers install it remotely until it works, with six security defaults done in one go: password changed, localhost-bound, permissions limited, skills whitelisted, API key secured, update plan in place. Want year-round support? Premium Annual or Annual Flagship.

# Remote OpenClaw Installation: Process, Security & How to Choose a Service

Think BIG Editorial

Want someone to install OpenClaw remotely but worried about security? This guide covers only the remote installation itself: what the process looks like, what you'll see during the session, what we explicitly don't do — and five questions to ask any remote installation service before you hand over access.

Updated: 2026-08-31

People searching "someone to install OpenClaw remotely" usually have two concerns: they can't get it installed themselves, and they're not comfortable letting a stranger onto their computer. The first problem is easy — pay someone who knows how. The second concern is the real barrier: you're handing your screen to an engineer you've never met. What gives you reason to trust them?

This guide isn't about whether OpenClaw is worth using (that's covered in the [installation overview guide](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/guides/openclaw-daizhuang/)). It covers only the remote installation itself: what the process looks like, what you'll see during the session, what we explicitly don't do — and five questions to use as your checklist for evaluating any service you consider.

## What is remote installation? How is it different from following a tutorial?

Remote installation is straightforward: an engineer connects to your computer via remote desktop software and sets up OpenClaw end-to-end, verifies it works, and you watch the whole thing on your screen. You don't touch the terminal, and you don't decode English error messages.

The key difference from following a tutorial yourself is the engineer's judgment. Tutorials can only describe an ideal path, but every computer has different system versions, permission settings, and installed software. When an error appears mid-installation that isn't in the tutorial, that's where experience matters. Much of what you're paying for is that experience with the unexpected.

"Consulting" extends beyond installation: the installation is just the start. What workflows to hand to your AI assistant, what skills you need, how to manage costs — these questions come after installation. Our approach is to understand your needs before quoting a scope, and to quote before charging.

## Full process: from inquiry to completion

- Brief conversation first:  Tell us your computer environment (operating system, rough specs) and what you want the AI assistant to do. If the environment isn't suitable, we'll say so upfront — not after you've placed an order.

- Order placed, time scheduled:  Contact us and arrange a mutually convenient installation slot. Service hours: Monday to Friday, 10:00–24:00 (UTC+8).

- Remote connection established:  At the scheduled time, you open AnyDesk or DeskIn and share the session code with the engineer. The connection is established only with your permission — you can disconnect at any time.

- Full transparency during installation:  Every action the engineer takes happens on your screen. You can see what they open and what they change. When you need to log in to an account or authorize something, you do it yourself — the engineer guides you.

- Live sign-off:  After installation, we verify together that the AI assistant runs, responds, and that any connected integrations receive messages. The session ends only once this is confirmed.

- Session ends immediately after completion:  Remote access is disconnected as soon as installation is done. No backdoor software is left on your computer. After that, contacting us is initiated by you — we don't have residual access.

After completion, the Persona Edition includes 7-day post-installation technical support, a full personal skill package + 1 custom helper + Coding Agent connection. Ready to use immediately.

## Security and trust: what we explicitly don't do

When someone connects remotely to your computer, the real concern isn't "will they install things wrong" — it's "what else did they do?" So rather than tell you to trust us, here's a written list of boundaries you can verify item by item:

- We never ask for passwords or credentials.  Any login needed is performed by you. Passwords and API keys are never transmitted via any chat message.

- We don't apply for or manage your API keys.  When a cloud-based large model is used, the AI model key is applied for by you. The engineer guides you verbally. The key is yours — it goes into your computer's local config file only. We never handle it or retain it. Local version: no API key needed.

- Keys are not pushed to any cloud version control.  Nothing of yours is committed to any cloud repository during the installation.

- AnyDesk or DeskIn only.  We don't accept other remote software, don't use SSH direct connections, and don't do on-site installations. We insist on these two tools because: the connection requires your permission, you can see everything throughout, and sessions are traceable.

- Official release only.  OpenClaw is installed from the official source — not third-party redistributions.

- Session ends at completion — no backdoors left.  Worth repeating.

All of the above is standard practice across all plans — no surcharge. If you need supply-chain scanning or 24-hour monitoring as enterprise-grade security measures, that falls under custom scope and can be discussed separately.

## How to evaluate a remote installation service: five checkpoints

This section isn't only for people considering us. The market has multiple services offering OpenClaw installation. Regardless of who you go with, ask them these five questions first:

- What tool do you use to connect?  The answer should be a named, mainstream remote desktop application (such as AnyDesk or DeskIn) where you grant permission and can disconnect. If they want your SSH credentials or want you to install an unfamiliar connection program, choose someone else.

- Will you ever ask for my passwords or API keys?  The proper approach is for you to enter them yourself, with the key stored only on your machine. Anyone who asks you to paste credentials into a chat should be immediately disqualified.

- Can you still access my computer after installation?  The answer should be "no — only if you allow a new session." Ask explicitly whether anything is left behind for persistent remote access.

- Have you separated the service fee from AI model usage fees?  Model fees are billed per use, paid directly by you — if the service provider doesn't mention this proactively, factor that into how you weigh their other claims.

- Is it the official release?  Ask "where does the version you're installing come from?" If they can't answer or give a vague answer, the risk is yours to judge.

We operate exactly according to these five criteria, so we're comfortable publishing them as a public checklist. Use them on us or on any other provider.

## Pricing: two separate costs

The fee structure for remote installation has exactly two parts — keeping them clear prevents any unpleasant surprises:

- Service fee:  Paid to us, one-time, no monthly subscription. The Persona Edition AI Assistant is priced on request and includes environment setup, supportive or challenging personality selection, full personal skill package + 1 custom helper, Coding Agent connection, and 7-day technical support.

- AI model usage fee (cloud version only):  When using cloud-based large models, usage fees are paid to the model provider based on actual usage — independent of us and not included in the service fee. Local version: no model usage fees.

Add-on skill packages later are sold in three tiers: 10, 20, or 40 packs (priced on request). Before purchase, an engineer evaluates how many skills your use case needs, then maps it to the appropriate tier — to avoid buying too few or overspending.

If the installation cannot be completed due to an issue on our side, we provide a full refund in accordance with applicable consumer protection regulations.

## After installation: what consulting support covers

Installation solves "can't get it set up." Consulting support solves "it's installed but I don't know how to use it effectively." The typical path looks like:

- Run the standard installed skills for a while  to understand what repetitive work you actually do every day.

- When specific needs emerge, add skill packages  — the engineer builds your specific workflows (auto-replies, quotes, scheduled reminders) as custom skills.

- If you don't want to maintain it yourself, consider an annual plan  — the engineer provides ongoing support, updates, and maintenance.

Needs first, specs second. We don't recommend buying to the ceiling from day one. Get the Persona Edition working and develop a feel for it; then your money goes exactly where it's needed.

## Rolled Out AI and Nobody Uses It? The Problem Usually Isn't the AI. Work Backward From the One Task Employees Actually Do Every Day

Think BIG Content Team  |  October 21, 2026

When AI rollouts go unused, it's rarely because the model isn't smart enough. More often, nobody decided what it was for, nobody showed employees how to use it, and it never made it into the daily work. The fix: work backward from one task employees actually do every day.

## 1.  What's happening: bought, installed, activated, and then ignored

Plenty of companies have been through this. The boss sees how impressive AI is, buys a tool, sets up accounts, and holds a kickoff session. Two or three weeks later, employees are still doing things the old way, and hardly anyone clicks into the AI.

It isn't just a few companies. Surveys in Taiwan and abroad show the same pattern:

Taiwan: the biggest roadblock is "we don't know what to use it for."  As reported by Taiwanese media, the 2025 Survey on AI Use Among Small and Medium Enterprises , commissioned by Taiwan's Small and Medium Enterprise and Startup Administration (Ministry of Economic Affairs) and conducted by the Industrial Technology Research Institute, collected 1,207 valid responses from companies with 199 or fewer employees. The top challenge SMEs cited when considering AI was "no clear use case yet," followed by not understanding AI, high costs, talent shortages, and difficulty measuring results. The same survey found that only about 15% of SMEs have AI talent, and roughly 75% of that talent are entry-level users of off-the-shelf tools. (Source: [China Times Want Rich, 2025-12-26](https://wantrich.chinatimes.com/news/20251226900494-420501))

Globally: most companies haven't seen results yet.  An international management consulting firm surveyed 1,000 senior executives in 2024 and found that 74% of companies had yet to show tangible value from AI. Only 26% had built the capabilities to move beyond proofs of concept and generate real value. (Source: [BCG press release, 2024-10-24](https://www.bcg.com/press/24october2024-ai-adoption-in-2024-74-of-companies-struggle-to-achieve-and-scale-value))

People are using AI, just not the company's.  A large software company's 2024 survey of 31,000 knowledge workers in 31 markets found that 75% already use generative AI at work, but 78% of those users bring their own AI tools. Only 39% of people who use AI at work have received AI training from their company. (Source: [Microsoft Work Trend Index 2024](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/worklab/work-trend-index/ai-at-work-is-here-now-comes-the-hard-part))

Put the three together and the picture is clear: employees aren't refusing AI. The setup their company handed them just doesn't connect to the work they actually do every day.

## 2.  The debate: is the problem the AI, or the people and processes?

Those who say it's about processes and organization  have plenty of evidence. In the same report, the consulting firm describes a "10-20-70" principle: leading companies put 10% of their resources into algorithms, 20% into technology and data, and 70% into people and processes. (Source: [BCG press release](https://www.bcg.com/press/24october2024-ai-adoption-in-2024-74-of-companies-struggle-to-achieve-and-scale-value))

A 2025 preliminary report from a research initiative at MIT reached a similar conclusion. As reported by Fortune , it found that most companies' generative AI efforts were falling short, and that the key issue wasn't the quality of the AI models but a "learning gap" between tools and organizations, along with flawed enterprise integration. (Source: [Fortune, 2025-08-18](https://fortune.com/2025/08/18/mit-report-95-percent-generative-ai-pilots-at-companies-failing-cfo/))

Skeptics raise two cautions:  1. Read the numbers carefully.  The MIT report is preliminary research, and coverage describes its sample and methods inconsistently. It shouldn't be taken as proof that every AI project fails. 2. Tools still matter.  If an AI often gets answers wrong, gives no sources, or responds slowly, employees will try it once or twice and stop. No amount of training can save a tool that isn't good enough.

The two views don't conflict: a good-enough tool is the baseline. Once you clear that bar, what decides whether people use it is where it's used, who uses it, and how.

◆ First-hand notes

## 3. What we've learned doing this work

Think BIG deploys AI agents for businesses and keeps reviewing usage logs after handover. Here's what we've learned, with no client details:

1. Unused systems all show similar symptoms.  Employees stick with the old way. They ask once, get a wrong answer, and never ask again. The entry point is buried behind several logins. Nobody knows what to ask. Answers come without sources, so people don't dare rely on them. Permissions are misconfigured, so people can't see documents they should. Almost none of this has anything to do with how smart the model is.

2. Work backward from one task, not forward from a pile of features.  Before we start, we look for a task that meets three conditions: it happens every day, its rules can be written down, and the cost of a wrong answer is manageable. Think "sales looking up product specs" or "new hires checking internal policies." Get that one task used every day first, then move to the second.

3. Write acceptance questions the way employees actually ask.  We prepare a set of acceptance questions with known answers, phrased as closely as possible to how employees really talk, including abbreviations, casual wording, even typos. A system that aces neatly worded test questions but stumbles on real ones is a very common gap.

4. Put the AI where employees already are.  Every new website or account adds friction. When the AI lives inside a chat tool or system employees already use daily, usage tends to be much better. One caveat: when you connect an outside chat channel such as LINE, messages through that channel pass through that service, so make that clear before rollout.

5. Say "I don't know" when it doesn't know, and cite sources when it does.  Whether employees use it comes down to trust. When an answer shows which document it came from, employees can click through and check. Saying "I couldn't find that" builds more trust than making something up.

6. After handover, review the logs every week.  What employees asked, which questions got weak answers, which documents need to be added: it's all in the logs. Name one internal point person to spend a little time each week reviewing logs and adding material, and the system gets more accurate the more it's used. That's also the most practical way to close the "learning gap" mentioned above.

Our biggest takeaway: whether an AI rollout succeeds is often decided before the work begins.  Get clear on which one task the AI is for, and most of the later problems disappear.

## 4.  Our recommendations: answer these five questions before you roll out

1. What's the most time-consuming, most annoying task employees do every day?  Ask the front line directly, not just managers. 2. Does that task follow rules?  Work with documentation and standard answers is the best first job for an AI agent. 3. What happens if the answer is wrong?  Start with tasks where mistakes are manageable. For high-stakes work like external quotes or legal judgments, have the AI draft and a person confirm. 4. Where will employees use it?  Put it inside tools they already use, and open as few new entry points as possible. 5. Who reviews the logs and adds material?  Name one internal point person. They don't need to be technical, but they need to know the process and be able to make decisions.

Start with features Work backward from one task
Starting point What the tool can do What frustrates employees every day

First month Lots of features; nobody knows where to start One task used by someone every day

Acceptance Judged on the demo Tested with questions employees actually ask

After handover Nobody reviews logs; usage fades Weekly log reviews and new material; it gets more accurate over time

Bottom line: if nobody uses your AI, don't swap the AI first. Swap the question.

Further reading: if nobody inside your company can own the work of wiring AI into your processes, see [Think BIG NEWS Issue 007, "What Is a Forward Deployed Engineer?"](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/news/fde-outsourced-engineer-20261013/), on how small businesses can fill that gap with an embedded-style approach.

◆ Editor's Note · How Think BIG Approaches This

## Start with one task. Frozen scope. Delivery within 30 days.

(The following reflects Think BIG's own position and is separate from the neutral reporting above.)

We act as a company's remote FDE (embedded engineering) team, using TB FRAME, our four-stage method (assess, build, verify, maintain), to wire AI agents into your work: Start with one task:  during assessment, we identify the one rule-based task employees actually do every day, then decide what the AI agent will and won't do. Frozen scope, delivery within 30 days:  scope and acceptance questions are written down before work starts, and delivery happens within 30 days once scope is frozen and data is in place. Acceptance in your employees' words:  we test against known answers before handover; answers cite sources, and the agent says "I don't know" when it can't find something. First year of maintenance:  all three plans include first-year maintenance; after handover, we keep reviewing logs, adding material, and sending proactive alerts.

We don't promise sales results. We promise to wire AI into your actual work and let you see that it's running.

### FAQ

Q1: Why don't employees use AI after the company rolls it out?
The most common reason isn't that the AI isn't smart enough. It's that nobody decided which task the AI was for, nobody taught employees how to use it, and it never became part of the daily workflow. Answers without sources and hard-to-find entry points also make employees give up after a try or two.
Q2: What's the biggest barrier to AI adoption for small businesses in Taiwan?
According to media reports on the 2025 Survey on AI Use Among Small and Medium Enterprises, commissioned by Taiwan's Small and Medium Enterprise and Startup Administration and conducted by the Industrial Technology Research Institute, the top challenge SMEs cite when considering AI is "no clear use case yet," followed by not understanding AI, high costs, talent shortages, and difficulty measuring results.
Q3: Where should an AI rollout start?
With one task: find work employees repeat every day, whose rules can be written down, and where a wrong answer is manageable, such as looking up product specs or internal policies. Get that task used every day, then expand to a second.
Q4: How can you tell whether an AI rollout actually worked?
Don't judge by the demo. Build acceptance questions in the words employees really use, and confirm that answers are correct, cite sources, and say "I don't know" when nothing is found. After handover, keep reviewing usage logs to see whether people use it and which questions get weak answers.
Q5: Will employees avoid AI because they're worried about their jobs?
They might, which is why communication matters. Start with the repetitive, time-consuming work employees find most frustrating, so the AI saves them time, rather than starting with work that depends on their professional judgment. When employees see AI lightening their own load, they're usually much more willing to use it.

# AI Is Being Used to Automate Attacks — Could Your Tools Become Someone Else's Entry Point? | Think BIG NEWS

Field Notes · Issue 010
