Q26

# How Long Does a Custom Picture Book Take? How to Plan the Order Before a Holiday

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-11-05
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/custom-book-lead-time/)

The short answer

To estimate when a custom picture book will arrive, add four segments in order: (1) payment and photo submission, (2) preview confirmation, (3) production time, (4) shipping time. Depending on how quickly each step proceeds and the provider's schedule, the total time varies; it is safest to place the order at least two weeks before you need the book. The specific start date for production and what counts as a working day depend on the provider's terms.

## 1. Four segments for scheduling

Regardless of provider, the production timeline generally includes these four segments:

Segment 1: Payment and photo submission.  After placing the order and paying, read the provider's photo usage instructions, then submit the photos. How long this takes depends on when you have the photos ready.

Segment 2: Preview confirmation.  The provider generates a preview (usually the cover and some interior pages) for you to check the character's appearance and text. How long this segment takes depends on how quickly both sides respond; if revisions are needed, it may take longer.

Segment 3: Production time.  After confirming the preview, the provider starts production. Working days are usually specified in the terms; whether weekends and holidays are included varies by provider.

Segment 4: Shipping time.  After production is complete, the book is shipped via the logistics provider; delivery time depends on the logistics provider's schedule.

## 2. Add buffer for important dates

For birthday gifts, holiday gifts, or books that need to arrive by a specific date, it is recommended to add at least 3–5 extra working days as a buffer in addition to the estimated schedule. Order early enough that even if each step takes a bit longer than expected, the book can still arrive on time.

If the gift will be shipped directly to the recipient, also confirm whether the recipient will be home to receive it, and arrange the delivery accordingly.

## 3. What to check before ordering

Before ordering, it is recommended to confirm: when does the production clock start (from payment, photo submission, or preview confirmation)? Do working days include weekends and public holidays? What is the estimated shipping time after production is complete? These answers affect the actual arrival date.

# What Photos Should I Take for a Custom Picture Book? 5 Tips for a Clear Face | Think BIG Q&A Library

Q18

# What Photos Should I Take for a Custom Picture Book? 5 Tips for a Clear Face

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-28
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/custom-book-photo-tips/)

The short answer

The key to a photo that produces a clear AI illustration is "face forward, well-lit, only this child." The Ministry of Foreign Affairs' passport photo guidelines (2025-08-29) specify: neutral expression facing the camera, full face visible, eyes open and looking at the lens, uniform light background, good lighting, no shadows on the face. These are also good benchmarks for custom picture book photos.

## 1. Five tips for taking the photo

Tip Home practice Passport photo benchmark
1. Face forward Ask the child to look at the camera; call their name or use a small toy to get their attention. Full face visible, facing forward, eyes looking at the lens.

2. Good lighting Use natural light from a window, stand facing the window; avoid backlighting or strong side shadows. Even lighting, no shadows on the face.

3. Only the child Move other people and large objects out of frame; keep the background simple. Only the applicant; a simple, uniform, light-colored background.

4. Eyes open Wait for the child to look up naturally; for young children, try after waking from a nap. Eyes open and clearly visible.

5. Clear, not blurry Keep the camera steady; for a smartphone, use the rear camera (usually higher resolution). Photo must be clear, without distortion or blurriness.

Passport photo standards come from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) 2025-08-29 guidelines; the right column's home practice descriptions are written based on these standards and are not official text. ([MOFA Passport Photo Specifications](https://www.boca.gov.tw/cp-56-4486-7bfab-1.html))

## 2. How many photos to provide

Providing 1–3 photos is usually sufficient. Multiple photos of the same face from different angles help the AI capture features more accurately. If the provider's instructions say a specific number, follow those instructions.

## 3. What if the existing photos aren't ideal?

If you don't have a suitable photo, taking a new one is an option. Find good natural light, let the child sit in a chair, hold a small toy to attract their gaze, and take several shots. A recent photo (taken within the past six months) is recommended, as the child's appearance changes quickly.

After receiving the photos, a preview (cover and some interior pages) is generated for confirmation; each order may regenerate the entire book once at no charge. Photos are deleted within 3 days of the book being delivered.

- Specifications:  21 × 21 cm, 26 interior pages, Chinese with phonetic notation (optional English); Style A watercolor album or Style B figurine 3D edition; NT$1,500 per book, domestic Taiwan shipping included; approximately 4 working days to produce, then shipped. Orders are not accepted on the official website—please order on Shopee.

See the [ordering process](https://talewithyoutw.com/how-it-works.html). Illustrations may not be identical to the person; a preview will be sent for confirmation before printing.

# Can I Return a Custom Picture Book? The 7-Day Cooling-Off Period and Its Exceptions | Think BIG Q&A Library

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Shared Reading & Custom Picture Books
Q07

# Can I Return a Custom Picture Book? The 7-Day Cooling-Off Period and Its Exceptions

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-17
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/custom-book-return-policy/)

The short answer

Most custom picture books do not qualify for the seven-day inspection period. Consumer Protection Act Article 19 gives online shoppers the right to cancel within 7 days of receiving a product without giving a reason, but the Executive Yuan's Regulations Governing Reasonable Exceptions to the Right of Rescission in Distance Transactions Article 2 lists "customized products made at the consumer's request" as an exception, provided the business notifies the consumer in advance. Not qualifying for the seven-day inspection period does not mean there is no recourse if a defective product is received: if the book has defects, rescission or a price reduction can still be requested under the Civil Code.

## 1. What is the seven-day inspection period

Consumer Protection Act Article 19 provides that consumers in distance transactions (online shopping, TV shopping, etc.) may rescind the contract within seven days of receiving the product by returning the product or giving written notice, without stating a reason and without bearing any cost . However, the same article also includes a proviso: "distance transactions with reasonable exceptional circumstances are not subject to this," with the exceptions set by the Executive Yuan. ([Consumer Protection Act](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=J0170001))

The same article contains another protection that is often overlooked: if the business fails to provide the information related to rescission as required, the seven-day period starts from the day after the information is provided, up to a maximum of four months.

## 2. Why custom products are an exception

The Regulations Governing Reasonable Exceptions to the Right of Rescission in Distance Transactions Article 2 lists 7 types of exceptions, the second of which is "customized products made at the consumer's request." ([Regulations Governing Reasonable Exceptions](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=J0170012)) A book made according to your child's photos and name cannot be sold to anyone else after it is made, so it falls into this category.

However, the regulations explicitly state the prerequisite: these exceptions only exclude the seven-day inspection period if the consumer has been notified by the business . So before placing the order, the business should clearly tell you "this is a custom product and does not qualify for the seven-day inspection period."

## 3. Even without no-reason returns, there are still these protections

Defects are handled separately.  Civil Code Article 354 requires the seller to guarantee that the product is free from defects that reduce its value or utility; Article 359 provides that in the event of defects, the buyer may rescind the contract or request a price reduction. ([Civil Code](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=B0000001)) Missing pages, printing errors, and binding failures are separate from the "seven-day inspection period."

Advertisements count.  Consumer Protection Act Article 22 requires businesses to ensure the accuracy of advertising content, and their obligations to consumers may not fall below the advertising content. The dimensions, page count, and content described on the product page are things you can demand.

Disputes can be reported.  First contact the business's customer service; if that fails, call the National Consumer Service Hotline at 1950, or file a complaint with the consumer service center of your local county or city government. ([Executive Yuan Consumer Protection Commission](https://cpc.ey.gov.tw/))

## 4. 4 things to check before ordering

1. Is it clearly stated that the seven-day inspection period does not apply?  Written in a place visible before checkout, not buried in long terms.

2. Can the order be cancelled before printing and what is the refund process?  Custom products are usually "once printed, cannot be cancelled"—so what about before printing?

3. Is there a preview before printing? How many revisions are allowed?  Seeing the preview before printing is the most practical protection for custom products.

4. How are defects handled?  What counts as a defect, whether reprinting requires shipping fees, and within what period you must contact them.

Brand information | Tale With You

## Tale With You's cancellation and refund policy

Tale With You's [Terms of Service](https://talewithyoutw.com/terms.html) (v1.3, updated October 10, 2026) addresses these 4 things:

- Notification:  Each book is individually produced based on the child's photos, nickname, and theme; in accordance with Consumer Protection Act Article 19 and Regulations Article 2(2), it does not qualify for the seven-day inspection period, with notification provided via a separate checkbox at the time of ordering.

- Cancellation before printing:  The order may be cancelled and a full refund given at any time before the book is sent to print.

- Preview and regeneration:  A preview (cover and some interior pages, low resolution with watermark) is sent first; printing proceeds only after confirmation; each order may regenerate the entire book once at no charge.

- Defects:  Damage, missing pages, incorrect page order, blurry printing, significant color deviation, or content different from the confirmed preview: free reprint with replacement (including shipping); reprinting requires re-uploading photos; if you prefer not to re-upload, a refund is available.

Cancellations and refunds for Shopee orders are processed according to Shopee's platform rules; where the terms differ from platform rules, the provision more favorable to the consumer applies.

Content in this section is taken from the Tale With You website [Terms of Service](https://talewithyoutw.com/terms.html), updated 2026-10-11. All characters in books and videos are AI-generated.

## FAQ

Q1: Do custom products qualify for the seven-day inspection period? Usually not. Consumer Protection Act Article 19 gives online shoppers a 7-day no-reason right of rescission, but the Regulations Governing Reasonable Exceptions Article 2(2) lists "customized products made at the consumer's request" as an exception, provided the business notifies the consumer in advance. Q2: If the business doesn't state that the seven-day inspection period doesn't apply, can I still return it? The regulations state that the exception only excludes the seven-day inspection period if the consumer is notified by the business. If the business did not notify in advance, it cannot claim this exception. Q3: What do I do if the custom picture book I received has defects? Defects and the seven-day inspection period are separate matters. Under Civil Code Articles 354 and 359, if a product has defects, the buyer may rescind the contract or request a price reduction; you may also first request a reprint under the business's defect handling policy. Q4: Can a Tale With You order be cancelled? An order can be cancelled before printing. Under Tale With You's Terms of Service v1.3, cancellation and full refund are available at any time before the book is sent to print; already-printed custom products cannot be cancelled, but printing defects are eligible for a free reprint.

# How Long Should a Child Practice Mandarin Each Day? One Long Session or a Little Every Day | Q&A Library | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

熊好學 · BearSay Mandarin BS02

# How Long Should a Child Practice Mandarin Each Day? One Long Session or a Little Every Day

Think BIG Q&A Library　·　November 9, 2026 　·　[中文版](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/daily-practice-spaced-review/)

Short answer

No reliable study sets a number of minutes per day that a child should practice Mandarin, so there is no fixed length to aim for. Cepeda and colleagues (2006) reviewed 317 experiments (839 comparisons) and found that splitting learning into separate sessions with gaps in between, called distributed practice, works best when the gap matches how long you want to remember: the longer the target, the longer the best gap. A steadier approach is short, regular repetition rather than one long catch-up session on the weekend. Most of those experiments tested adult word recall, so apply the idea to children with flexibility.

## 1. What the research says

Cepeda, Pashler, Vul, Wixted and Rohrer (2006) combined 184 articles, 317 experiments and 839 comparisons on the distributed practice effect: for the same amount of study, is it better to learn in one block, or in several sessions with a gap? They found that the review gap giving the best recall changes with the retention interval: the longer you want to remember, the longer the best gap. ([Psychological Bulletin, 2006](https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.132.3.354))

## 2. Limits of this finding

Mostly word-recall tasks.  The review is titled "verbal recall tasks." It is not about pronunciation, conversation or reading.

No minutes per day for children.  The review describes how gaps relate to retention. It gives no timetable for preschoolers or primary-school children, so this page does not give fixed minutes either.

A child's attention limits the length of one session.  Pushing a session until the child loses interest does not help. Stop while the child is still willing to speak.

## 3. How to use it at home

1. Short and regular.  Pick the same time each day for a small piece, such as one word or one sentence. This is easier to keep than a long weekly session.

2. Ask again a few days later.  Two or three days after a word is introduced, bring it up in a real situation. If the child cannot recall it, model it again without blame.

3. Repeat in different settings.  The same word at dinner, on the way out and in a picture book feels more like real use than copying one page ten times.

4. Do not chase an unbroken streak.  Missing a day does not undo progress. Continue the next day.

Brand information | BearSay Mandarin

## The daily word and spaced review

BearSay Mandarin (熊好學) is a learning brand for Taiwan Mandarin. Every day it teaches one Taiwan Mandarin word on Instagram ([@bearsaymandarin](https://www.instagram.com/bearsaymandarin/)), in Traditional characters with zhuyin and pinyin and multilingual subtitles, guided by five characters: BUBU, MIBO, HUBO, GUIBO and LANBO. The app is in development and has not been released. Release information will appear on the [BearSay Mandarin Q&A overview](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/bearsay/).

BearSay Mandarin currently publishes one word a day, which parents can treat as a regular touchpoint. How often to review, and for how long, is up to the family. BearSay Mandarin does not guarantee any learning result.

Source: the public Instagram account and this site's brand overview, updated 2026-11-09. Demo audio is AI-synthesized speech; BearSay Mandarin characters are AI-generated.

## Frequently asked questions

Q1: How long should a child practice Mandarin each day? No reliable study sets minutes per day for children. A steadier approach is short, regular repetition, ending while the child is still willing to speak. Q2: Is spaced practice better than cramming? Cepeda and colleagues (2006) reviewed 317 experiments and found that the best gap between study sessions depends on how long you want to remember: the longer the target, the longer the best gap. The experiments were mostly word recall with adults. Q3: How long should I wait before reviewing a word? There is no fixed number of days that fits every child. The research only shows that the gap should grow with the retention goal. At home you can start by asking again in a real situation two or three days later, then adjust. Q4: Does missing a day undo progress? No. Spaced practice is done in separate sessions anyway, so continue the next day.

Sources (links checked 2026-11-09)

- Cepeda, Pashler, Vul, Wixted & Rohrer (2006). Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis. Psychological Bulletin, 132(3), 354–380: [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.132.3.354)

# How Should a Company Classify Data Before Using AI? | Q&A Library | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Enterprise AI Security
TB27

# How Should a Company Classify Data Before Using AI?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-11-09
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/data-classification-for-ai/)

The short answer

Classify company data by the potential impact of disclosure, alteration, or loss of access, then decide which AI environments may process it. No universal chart settles cloud use for every company: purpose, contracts, law, and service settings matter. Local processing is an option, with access and outbound connections still controlled.

## 1. Assess consequences before assigning labels

NIST FIPS 199 (2004) categorizes information and systems by potential impacts on confidentiality, integrity, and availability. It is a US federal standard; this article borrows its risk reasoning rather than presenting it as a requirement for Taiwan businesses.

Ask who would be harmed by unauthorized access, who might act on an incorrect change, and which work would stop during an outage. We suggest business owners define the consequences, with security and legal review. File names and employee guesses do not create an operational policy.

## 2. Connect classification to permitted handling

These are proposed starting rules, not statutory categories or automatic permission to use an environment.

Situation
Suggested starting rule
Review needed
Approved public content
Assess approved external AI services
Version and purpose

Unpublished internal documents
Confirm recipients and permitted fields
Owner and retention terms

Personal, contract-restricted, or confidential data
Withhold from unapproved external tools
Legal, security, and data owner

Passwords and keys
Keep out of ordinary prompts
Controlled credential handling

OWASP LLM02:2025 identifies personal data, confidential business information, and credentials as sensitive and recommends least-privilege access. Consider retrieval, answer visibility, and logs as well as input.

We suggest treating mixed documents according to their more restricted content, or extracting approved portions. A public cover page does not authorize transmitting attachments or hidden fields.

## 3. Name owners and an exception process

Article 5 of Taiwan’s Personal Data Protection Act requires processing and use to stay within the necessary scope of a specific purpose and bear a reasonable connection to that purpose. Deployment labels do not establish compliance. This is general information, not legal advice.

Write rules covering tools, permitted information, redaction, approvers, retention, and exceptions. Hold uncertain material for review. For RAG or Agents, test accounts with different access rights and disallowed inputs to check that policy is implemented.

Brand information | Think BIG

## Data and permission inventories at Think BIG

Think BIG helps companies deploy AI Agents in their own environments. Running on company hardware does not keep every connection local: cloud models, messaging platforms, and other external services can still receive requests.

- Map data flows first : Before deployment, identify data sources, processing locations, output recipients, logs, and backups. Assess deployment location and external connections separately.

- Set permissions for the task : Define read and write access using least privilege. A designated person decides on external sending, spending, and changes to production systems.

See [Trust](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/) and [Local AI and data sovereignty](https://thinkbigtw.com/guides/local-ai-data/).

The actual scope of Think BIG’s services follows what both parties confirm.

## FAQ

Q1: Must all personal data stay on-premises? This article cannot establish that rule. Review purpose, legal basis, contracts, and recipient terms. Q2: Is public material unrestricted? Check versions, purpose, and applicable rights; public availability does not authorize every use. Q3: What about mixed documents? Apply the more restrictive handling rule or extract approved portions after review. Q4: What if an employee cannot classify a file? Hold it back from unapproved tools and ask the data owner to clarify the handling rule.

# How Should Personal Data Be De-Identified Before Files Are Given to AI? | Q&A Library | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Enterprise AI Security
TB17

# How Should Personal Data Be De-Identified Before Files Are Given to AI?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-30
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/deidentify-before-ai/)

The short answer

Handle two kinds of data separately: direct identifiers (names, national ID numbers, phone numbers, email addresses, home addresses) are deleted or swapped for codes; indirect identifiers (birth dates, job titles, departments, rare diagnoses, combinations of time and place) are generalized or grouped, because combined they can still point to a person. Article 17 of the Enforcement Rules of Taiwan's Personal Data Protection Act describes "unable to identify a specific data subject" as personal data processed with codes, anonymization, partial concealment, or other means so that the specific individual cannot be identified. NIST SP 800-188 also warns that data with only names removed can be re-identified when matched with other data. The most effective approach: do not give the AI fields it does not need.

## 1. Direct and indirect identifiers

- Direct identifiers : Article 2 of the Personal Data Protection Act defines personal data as including data that can identify a person directly or indirectly. In practice, data that identifies someone on sight, such as names, national ID numbers, phone numbers, email addresses, and home addresses, counts as direct identifiers.

- Indirect identifiers : Article 3 of the Enforcement Rules explains that "identifiable indirectly" means the data alone cannot identify the person, but can once compared, combined, or linked with other data.

NIST SP 800-188 (September 2023) gives an example: a medical dataset with names and medical record numbers removed can still be re-identified if joined with another dataset of room numbers, times, and names. So NIST recommends avoiding the word "anonymization" and using "de-identification," with an assessment of re-identification risk.

## 2. Five steps before giving files to AI

Step
What to do
Example
1. Ask what the AI needs
Keep only the fields the task needs and delete whole columns that it does not
To have AI group complaint types, customer names and phone numbers are not needed

2. Handle direct identifiers
Delete them, or swap them for codes
"Wang Xiaoming" becomes "Customer A"; delete the national ID column entirely

3. Handle indirect identifiers
Generalize, group, and merge rare categories
Keep only the birth year; turn ages into ranges; merge one-person departments into "Other"

4. Check free text
Notes, email bodies, and meeting minutes often hide names, phone numbers, and addresses
Search for phone, email, and ID number patterns first, then spot-check by hand

5. Keep the mapping table separate
The table linking codes to real identities is never given to the AI and is stored under access control
Only the responsible person can open the mapping table

The steps arrange NIST SP 800-188's approach of removing direct identifiers and transforming quasi-identifiers into an order of work before data goes to AI.

## 3. Limits to keep in mind

- Coding is not the same as unidentifiable.  NIST notes that pseudonymization (swapping identities for codes) is commonly used so that records about the same person can be matched and, if needed, linked back to the person; as long as the mapping table exists, re-identification risk exists. When the company keeps the table, the data is still identifiable to the company.

- Check file metadata too.  Document authors, editors, and photo capture details can reveal identities.

- When de-identification is not possible, change where it is processed.  If the work truly needs identifiable data, it can be processed with an on-premises model so the data stays in the company. See [What are the advantages of a local LLM?](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/local-llm-advantages/)

LLM02 "Sensitive Information Disclosure" in OWASP's 2025 Top 10 for LLM applications also advises that LLM applications perform adequate data sanitization to prevent user data from entering the training model.

Brand information | Think BIG

## FAQ

Q1: How should personal data be handled before files are given to AI? Delete or code direct identifiers (names, national ID numbers, phone numbers, email, addresses); generalize or group indirect identifiers (birth dates, job titles, rare combinations); check free-text fields one by one; and keep the mapping table separately. Do not give the AI fields it does not need. Q2: Is removing names enough to de-identify data? Usually not. Under Article 3 of the Enforcement Rules of Taiwan's Personal Data Protection Act, data that can identify a specific person once compared or combined with other data is indirectly identifiable, and NIST SP 800-188 gives examples of data with names removed being re-identified. Q3: What does "unable to identify a specific data subject" mean in Taiwan's law? Article 17 of the Enforcement Rules explains it as personal data processed with codes, anonymization, partial concealment, or other means so that the specific individual cannot be identified. Q4: What is the difference between de-identification and anonymization? NIST SP 800-188 reserves "anonymization" for processes that cannot be reversed. Many de-identified datasets can be reversed once a matching dataset is found, so NIST recommends the term "de-identification" together with an assessment of re-identification risk.

# How to Do Dialogic Reading: A 5-Minute Guide for Parents | Think BIG Q&A Library

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Shared Reading & Custom Picture Books
Q13

# How to Do Dialogic Reading: A 5-Minute Guide for Parents

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-23
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/dialogic-reading-at-home/)

The short answer

Dialogic reading reverses the roles in shared reading: the child gradually learns to be the storyteller, and the adult becomes the listener and questioner. The approach is to invite the child to speak on each page using prompts, then respond with the four PEER steps: Prompt the child to say something, Evaluate what they said, Expand the sentence a little, and Repeat the prompt. The U.S. Department of Education's What Works Clearinghouse found that this method has a positive effect on oral expression in preschool children.

## 1. What is dialogic reading

What Works Clearinghouse (the evidence evaluation program of the U.S. Department of Education's Institute of Education Sciences) describes it as an interactive picture book shared reading method aimed at improving young children's language and literacy skills: during shared reading, the roles of adult and child are reversed, the child learns to be the storyteller, and the adult is an active listener and questioner. ([WWC Dialogic Reading Report, revised 2007](https://ies.ed.gov/ncee/WWC/Docs/InterventionReports/WWC_Dialogic_Reading_020807.pdf)) The same report indicates that this method was developed in the 1980s, with a 1988 study published by Whitehurst et al. ([Developmental Psychology 24(4)](https://doi.org/10.1037/0012-1649.24.4.552))

## 2. 5 question types: CROWD

Question type What the adult does Examples you can try at home
C Completion Leave a blank at the end of a sentence for the child to fill in. "The puppy ran and ran, all the way to…?"

R Recall Ask the child what happened in a book they have read before. "Where did the puppy go last time?"

O Open-ended Encourage the child to describe what is happening in the picture. "What do you see on this page?"

W Wh- questions Ask "what, where, who" questions about the picture. "What is this?" "Where is he?"

D Distancing Connect the pictures and words in the book to the child's experiences outside the book. "You've eaten cake before too, right?"

Question types are from the WWC report; the right column examples are written based on those types.

## 3. 4 steps: PEER

- P (Prompt):  Use one of the question types above to invite the child to say something about the book.

- E (Evaluate):  Evaluate the child's response and give them feedback.

- E (Expand):  Expand on what the child said. If the child says "puppy," you say "Yes, the white puppy is running."

- R (Repeat):  Prompt once more and let the child repeat the expanded sentence themselves.

The WWC report also notes that the more familiar the child is with a book, the less the adult reads and the more they listen, gradually moving to questions that require more thought, taking the child from "describing what is in the picture" to "thinking about what is happening in the picture and how it relates to their own experience."

## 4. How to fit this into 5 minutes

5 minutes is a practical arrangement, not a research-specified length: pick a book the child knows well, select only 2–3 pages, ask 1–2 questions per page, respond with PEER, and read the remaining pages normally or leave them for next time. Stop if the child loses interest; there is no need to work through the entire book.

## 5. How to interpret the evidence

The studies compiled by WWC include 4 that meet evidence standards and 1 that meets standards with reservations, covering more than 300 preschool children, most from economically disadvantaged families; the conclusion is that there is a positive effect on oral expression and no clear effect on phonics. (Same [WWC report](https://ies.ed.gov/ncee/WWC/Docs/InterventionReports/WWC_Dialogic_Reading_020807.pdf)) Taiwan's Ministry of Education Bookstart Reading Handbook also notes that when parents use dialogic reading and frequently ask open-ended questions, preschoolers' expressive language ability shows significant improvement after one month. ([Bookstart Reading Handbook](https://wwwacc.ntl.edu.tw/public/Attachment/16715141325.pdf)) The AAP's 2024 policy statement in Pediatrics encourages parents to have conversations with children centered around books and stories starting from infancy. ([Pediatrics 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39342414/))

Brand information | Tale With You

Tale With You's books have the same child as the main character on all 26 interior pages, illustrated based on the child's photos, with Tangyuan the puppy on every page and phonetic notation next to every Chinese character. For dialogic reading, you can start with a simple prompt like "find where Tangyuan is." Content in this section is taken from the Tale With You website's themes and samples page and FAQ, verified on 2026-10-15. All characters in books and videos are AI-generated.

## FAQ

Q1: What is dialogic reading? Dialogic reading is an interactive picture book shared reading method: the roles of adult and child are reversed, the child learns to be the storyteller, and the adult becomes the active listener and questioner. Q2: What does PEER stand for in dialogic reading? PEER is four steps: Prompt the child to say something about the book, Evaluate their response, Expand what they said to make the sentence longer, and Repeat the prompt to let them say the expanded sentence themselves. Q3: Is dialogic reading supported by research? Yes. The U.S. Department of Education's What Works Clearinghouse compiled 4 studies meeting evidence standards and 1 meeting standards with reservations, covering more than 300 preschool children; the conclusion is a positive effect on oral expression and no clear effect on phonics. Q4: How long should dialogic reading last? There is no fixed length. "5 minutes" is a practical arrangement: pick a familiar book, select 2–3 pages, ask 1–2 questions per page, and stop when the child loses interest.

- Whitehurst, G. J., Falco, F. L., Lonigan, C. J., et al. (1988). Accelerating language development through picture book reading. Developmental Psychology , 24(4), 552–559: [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1037/0012-1649.24.4.552)

# My Child Loves Dinosaurs: From a Picture Book to a Museum

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-31
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/dinosaur-loving-kids/)

The short answer

You can connect "book, museum, draw it at home" into a path: first learn about a few dinosaur species from books, then visit a museum to find the real specimens and fossils, then have the child draw what they saw when they get home. The National Museum of Natural Science in Taichung's Life Science Hall has a "Dinosaur Age" exhibit with a mechanical T. rex 7 meters long and 4 meters tall that moves and roars, as well as a Tarbosaurus skull, a juvenile T. rex skeleton, and more; the National Taiwan Museum in Taipei's Paleontology Gallery has the permanent exhibition "Great Paleontology Exhibition — The Epic of Life and the Dance of Evolution," featuring Huanghetitan, Tarbosaurus, Velociraptor, and other species.

## 1. Two national museums in Taiwan where you can see dinosaurs

Museum Location Dinosaur-related exhibits
National Museum of Natural Science
Life Science Hall No. 1, Guanqian Road, North District, Taichung City 1F "Dinosaur Age" exhibit: a mechanical T. rex 7 meters long and 4 meters tall that moves and roars, a pair of mechanical Velociraptors, Ankylosaur bones, a group burial fossil of Oviraptors, a Tarbosaurus skull, and a juvenile T. rex skeleton; the 2F has exhibits on what dinosaurs are and Archaeopteryx; the atrium displays pterosaurs overhead. ([NMNS Life Science Hall](https://www.nmns.edu.tw/ch/exhibitions/galleries/life-science-hall/))

National Taiwan Museum
Paleontology Gallery No. 25, Xiangyang Road, Zhongzheng District, Taipei City ([NTM](https://www.ntm.gov.tw/cp.aspx?n=5438)) Permanent exhibition "Great Paleontology Exhibition — The Epic of Life and the Dance of Evolution": the "Mesozoic Rulers" section features Huanghetitan, Tarbosaurus, and Velociraptor, as well as pterosaurs, ichthyosaurs, plesiosaurs, mosasaurs, and other Mesozoic reptiles. ([Ministry of Culture Arts Events Platform: NTM Great Paleontology Exhibition](https://event.culture.tw/mocweb/reg/NTM/Detail.init.ctr?actId=90081))

The NTM website lists the "Great Paleontology Exhibition" as a permanent exhibit in the Paleontology Gallery; ([NTM exhibition information](https://www.ntm.gov.tw/News_actives.aspx?n=5473&sms=13389&_CSN=2446)); the Ministry of Culture Arts Events Platform lists the exhibition period as through December 31, 2026. Opening hours, admission prices, and exhibits may change; please check each museum's official website for the latest announcements before visiting.

## 2. Before, during, and after the visit

Here are some practical suggestions:

Before: pick 3 "dinosaurs we're looking for today."  Choose the child's 3 favorites from a book; having a mission at the museum makes the visit more purposeful.

During: let the child be the tour guide.  Ask "what do you think it ate?" "Does it look the same as the one in the book?" Answers don't need to be correct; the goal is to get the child talking. For questioning techniques, see [How to do dialogic reading](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/dialogic-reading-at-home/).

After: draw it, then tell someone about it.  Have the child draw the dinosaur they saw on paper, then tell a family member about it.

## 3. Things you can discuss with the child while there

The NTM exhibition notes state that Earth has experienced at least five mass extinction events; and in Taiwan, the Penghu Channel and the Zuozhen area of Tainan have preserved large quantities of Pleistocene terrestrial vertebrate fossils, known as the "Penghu Fauna" and the "Zuozhen Fauna" respectively. ([NTM Great Paleontology Exhibition introduction](https://event.culture.tw/mocweb/reg/NTM/Detail.init.ctr?actId=90081)) These are not dinosaur fossils, but they can help children understand that the land of Taiwan has also buried animals from long ago.

# Does an AI Custom Book Look Like My Child? Why You Should Check the Preview Before Printing

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-11-09
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/does-ai-book-look-like-my-child/)

The short answer

AI custom picture book illustrations may differ from the actual person, so before printing you should check your own preview rather than relying only on the sample characters on the website. Using Tale With You's description as an example, illustrations are drawn referencing the photos, and a preview is sent before printing; parents can first check the character, name, and dedication, then request adjustments according to the service's rules. How many pages are in the preview and whether changes are still possible after confirmation should be asked in advance.

## 1. Turn "doesn't look like" into specific details that can be discussed

Tale With You's [FAQ](https://talewithyoutw.com/faq.html) explains that the main character is generated based on the photos, with the face, hair, and skin tone checked page by page; it also notes that illustrations may not be completely identical to the person. This is the brand's description of its production method, not an objective score of how similar each finished book will be.

When reviewing the preview, you can first write down the features you care about: the direction of the fringe, hair length, glasses, or face shape. If something seems off, it is recommended to use a specific description such as "the original photo shows hair to below the ear, but the preview shows it reaching the shoulder," and then ask the provider whether it can be addressed. These are examples of communication; they do not mean each item can be revised individually.

## 2. Review the preview in three rounds, don't rush to send confirmation

What to review Recommended approach Character Place the original photo beside it and first check the features you care about. If an adult also appears, have that person check their own illustration too.

Text Read the name, nickname, and dedication aloud word by word to check for any incorrect characters or wording that is not what the family intended.

Story and visuals Confirm whether the pages provided match the chosen theme; note any issues such as extra limbs or illegible text, and ask about each one.

It is recommended that one parent consolidate the feedback into a single message: "The issues I see are…, and I would like to confirm the range of adjustments that are possible…." If only some pages are shown in the preview, ask who checks the remaining pages and how issues with pages not shown are handled. Do not assume on your own that "having a preview" means every page can be reviewed individually.

Tale With You's [Terms of Service Article 4](https://talewithyoutw.com/terms.html) states that the preview is the cover and some interior pages; the name and dedication text may be revised before confirmation; each order may regenerate the entire book once at no charge. This rule is a full regeneration, not unlimited individual page revisions.

## 3. Also ask about the scope and method of confirmation

The brand's terms state that once "confirmed" is replied, the order enters printing and the content cannot be changed afterward. Therefore, if there are any questions, you can first write "I still want to confirm something here, please don't send to print yet," and wait for the provider's reply before deciding. This is a communication approach recommended in this article; the actual process is subject to the provider's confirmation.

It is also recommended to keep the confirmed images and text in an order record you can find, and to check with family members before sharing. According to the brand's [Privacy Policy](https://talewithyoutw.com/privacy.html), previews are low-resolution files with watermarks; the provider's own files and messages on platforms have different deletion scopes; do not assume the other party will keep all versions for you long-term.

For improving photo preparation, see [How to take a clear photo](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/custom-book-photo-tips/); for remaining questions about revisions, cancellations, and delivery times, first check the [pre-purchase checklist](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/how-to-choose-custom-book/).

If family members have differing opinions, it is recommended to first list the items you all care about, then ask about the scope of possible adjustments, to avoid missing any issues across multiple messages.

Brand information | Tale With You

## Tale With You's preview and regeneration rules

According to Tale With You's [FAQ](https://talewithyoutw.com/faq.html), the main character is generated based on the photos, with the face, hair, and skin tone checked page by page; illustrations may differ from the actual person, and a preview is sent before printing.

[Terms of Service Article 4](https://talewithyoutw.com/terms.html) explains that the preview consists of the cover and some interior pages, in low resolution with a watermark; parents confirm the character, name, and dedication, while the brand checks the remaining pages individually. Each order may regenerate the entire book once at no charge; once confirmation is replied, printing begins and the content cannot be changed afterward.

## FAQ

Q1: If the character doesn't look like the child, how do I describe it clearly? You can describe the specific differences between the original photo and the preview, then ask whether an adjustment is possible, rather than just writing "doesn't look like." Q2: If only the cover is received, does that count as reviewing the whole book? No. You should confirm the scope of the preview, how the pages not provided are checked, and how issues with pages not shown are handled. Q3: Should I ask the child to rate the preview? Not necessary. You can invite the child to look at the picture, but do not ask them to say it looks like them or that they are satisfied; the text and process of the order are confirmed by the parent. Q4: Does Tale With You's regeneration mean individual page revisions? The terms state that each order may regenerate the entire book once at no charge; revisions to the name and dedication text are unlimited before confirmation.

# Company Data in ChatGPT: Risks & Policy | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Enterprise AI Security
TB01

# What Are the Risks When Employees Paste Company Data into ChatGPT, and How Should a Company Manage It?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-19
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/employees-chatgpt-company-data/)

The short answer

The risk has two layers. Once data is pasted, it sits on the provider's servers (even if it is not used for training, it is retained for some time). And when employees use personal accounts, the company cannot control whether their chats are used for training. The answer is not a blanket ban but three steps: name the approved tools and company accounts, classify data and state which level may go where, and give confidential data a tool that does not send it outside the company.

## 1. Where does pasted data go?

When an employee presses send, the text goes to the provider's servers. Whether it is then stored or used for training depends on the plan. Official documentation as of 2026-10-19:

Usage
Used for model training?
Retention
ChatGPT personal accounts (Free, Go, Plus, Pro)
The user turns "Improve the model for everyone" on or off in Data controls; when off, new chats are not used for training
Chats stay in history; Temporary Chats may be retained up to 30 days for safety

ChatGPT Business, Enterprise and other managed workspaces
Not used for training by default, per OpenAI
Follows the workspace's retention settings

OpenAI API
Since March 1, 2023, API data is not used for training unless you opt in
Abuse monitoring logs retained up to 30 days by default

Anthropic (Claude) commercial products and API
Not used for training by default
API inputs and outputs deleted within 30 days by default, with exceptions

The point: "Is it used for training?" and "Is it retained?" are separate questions.  Even on a no-training plan, the data has left the company and stayed on someone else's servers for a while. For truly confidential material, the test is not whether training is off but whether the data may leave the company at all.

## 2. Legal points in Taiwan

If the pasted text contains personal data of customers or staff, Taiwan's Personal Data Protection Act may come into play:

- Article 5 : collection, processing, and use of personal data must not exceed what is necessary for the specific purpose.

- Article 20 : non-government entities must use personal data within the necessary scope of the specific purpose of collection.

- Article 4 : a party commissioned by a government or non-government entity to collect, process, or use personal data is treated as the commissioning party within the scope of the Act. Under Article 8 of the Act's Enforcement Rules, a party that commissions others to collect, process, or use personal data must properly supervise the commissioned party (for example, by agreeing on the scope of processing, security measures, and the return or deletion of data when the engagement ends, and by checking compliance regularly). In other words, if handing personal data to an outside service counts as commissioning under the Act, the company has a duty to supervise, and its responsibility does not pass to the provider just because the data was handed over. Whether pasting data into a particular AI service counts as commissioning depends on the facts, such as the service terms, the account type, and how the data is used.

For government agencies, the Executive Yuan presented the "Reference Guidelines for the Use of Generative AI by the Executive Yuan and Its Agencies" at its cabinet meeting on August 31, 2023. One aim is for agencies to maintain the confidentiality and professionalism of official business, and ministries are asked to set rules or internal controls for generative AI as their work requires. Private companies are not bound by it, but the direction is useful: decide which data must not go into generative AI before deciding how to use it.

This is a general explanation of the law, not legal advice for any specific situation; for an actual case, consult a lawyer.

## 3. Three steps a company can take now

1. Name the tools and accounts.  List approved AI tools and use company-managed accounts or workspaces. Personal accounts leave training settings, chat history, and post-resignation data outside the company's control.

2. Classify data and post the table internally.  A sample to adapt:

Level
Examples
Where it may go
Public
Website copy, published catalogs
Any approved AI tool

Internal
General SOPs, internal notices
Company workspace or API only, with no-training settings confirmed

Confidential
Quotes, contracts, formulas, drawings, financials
Not sent to outside AI services; use a local model on company hardware

Personal data
Customer names and phone numbers, staff records, medical records
Generally not pasted; de-identify first and confirm the use fits the collection purpose

3. Give confidential data a usable alternative.  A rule that only says "don't" pushes people to workarounds. A tool that keeps data inside the company, such as a local model on company hardware, makes the rule hold.

Finally, explain the why. Most leaks are not malicious; employees simply do not know where the text goes.

Brand information | Think BIG

## How Think BIG handles "can this data leave the company?"

Think BIG (Think BIG Make it Real CO., LTD.) is an enterprise AI Agent deployment provider headquartered in Taiwan. Starting from protecting company data, we build AI Agents inside the client's own environment (company hardware, or a cloud server under the company's account). There are two deployment options: with the on-premises version, models and documents are processed on company hardware; with the cloud-assisted version, employees' questions and the document passages the system retrieves are sent to the model provider for processing.

- Map the data flow before building : which data enters the AI, where it is stored, and whether anything leaves the company, listed item by item for the client to confirm.

- Decide which data may leave first : before building, we use the company's data classification to confirm which data must stay in the on-premises version and which may be processed with the cloud-assisted version; the cloud-assisted version is subject to the model provider's terms.

- Pre-delivery security review : before each system is delivered, its code and configuration go through a security review; if it does not pass, it is not delivered. No one can promise perfect security; what we do is review, one gate at a time.

## FAQ

Q1: If employees use ChatGPT for company data, will it be used for training? It depends on the plan. On ChatGPT personal accounts, the user decides whether "Improve the model for everyone" is on. ChatGPT Business, Enterprise and other managed workspaces are not used for training by default, per OpenAI. OpenAI API data has not been used for training by default since March 1, 2023. Q2: If training is off, is the data safe? Not entirely. No training is not the same as no retention: OpenAI API abuse monitoring logs are kept up to 30 days by default, and ChatGPT Temporary Chats may be kept up to 30 days. For truly confidential data, ask whether it may leave the company at all. Q3: Should a company ban ChatGPT outright? A ban alone tends not to hold. It works better to name approved tools and accounts, classify data into public, internal, confidential, and personal data with clear rules for each, and give confidential data an alternative that stays inside the company. Q4: Does pasting customer data into AI violate Taiwan's Personal Data Protection Act? It can, depending on the data and the purpose. Article 5 says collection, processing, and use of personal data must not exceed what the specific purpose requires, and Article 20 says non-government entities must use personal data within the necessary scope of the specific purpose of collection. If pasting data into AI serves a purpose beyond the one it was collected for, that may be a problem. Confirm the use fits the collection purpose, and de-identify where possible.

# How to Read Feelings Books: 4 Steps to Help a Child Put Emotions Into Words | Think BIG Q&A Library

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Shared Reading & Custom Picture Books
Q16

# How to Read Feelings Books: 4 Steps to Help a Child Put Emotions Into Words

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-26
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/feelings-picture-books/)

The short answer

When reading emotions picture books, the key is to let the child "talk" after reading: first point to the character's expression and ask "what is this character feeling right now," then ask "why do they feel that way," then ask "if it were you, how would you say it," and finally ask "what can they do to feel better." These 4 steps correspond to the four abilities of the emotions domain in the Ministry of Education's Preschool Curriculum Framework: awareness and identification, understanding, expression, and regulation; the framework also lists characters in stories and videos as one of the objects through which young children practice emotions.

## 1. What the curriculum framework says about emotional abilities

The Ministry of Education's Preschool Curriculum Framework, promulgated December 1, 2016, lists emotions as one of six domains and divides the ability to handle emotions into four categories. ([Ministry of Education Legal Information](https://edu.law.moe.gov.tw/LawContent.aspx?id=GL001586)):

- Awareness and identification:  When an emotion arises, being able to identify what emotion it is.

- Understanding:  Figuring out what happened and what one thinks about it.

- Expression:  Understanding the rules of one's cultural context and expressing emotions at appropriate times, in appropriate situations, and in appropriate roles.

- Regulation:  Using various strategies to change negative or overly intense emotions.

The framework divides learning into two dimensions: "self" and "others and environment." The "environment" in "others and environment" refers to the emotional responses that young children project onto animals, objects, texts and videos  in their environment—that is, anthropomorphized characters in stories and videos. In other words, the framework also lists characters in stories and videos as objects through which young children practice emotions.

The framework also notes that both positive and negative emotions have reasons for appearing and are worth exploring; what young children need to learn is to accept their emotions, not to deny them.

## 2. 4 steps for reading an emotions picture book

Step What you can say Corresponding ability
1. Find the expression "Look at their eyebrows and mouth—what are they feeling right now?" Awareness and identification

2. Say the reason "Why are they angry? What just happened?" Understanding

3. Try a different way to say it "If you were them, how would you tell your friend?" Expression

4. Think of a solution "What can they do to feel better?" Regulation

The ability names and categories come from the curriculum framework; the steps and questions in the left two columns are designed based on these four abilities as a way to do shared reading—they are not the original text of the framework.

The framework notes that young children's learning about emotions typically starts with themselves and gradually expands to others and objects in the environment. So after reading about the character's feelings, you can turn the question back to the child: "When do you feel scared?"

## 3. Things to keep in mind while reading

Don't rush to teach a lesson.  If the child says "they're very angry," first respond "right, they're very angry," rather than immediately adding "being angry is bad." This echoes the framework's direction of "accepting emotions rather than denying them."

Only discuss one or two pages at a time.  This is a practical recommendation: pick the page with the most obvious expression, and read normally if the child doesn't want to discuss. For questioning techniques, see [How to do dialogic reading](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/dialogic-reading-at-home/).

Shared reading itself is beneficial.  The AAP's 2024 policy statement in Pediatrics notes that shared reading strengthens the parent-child relationship and is one of the foundations of children's social-emotional, cognitive, language, and literacy development. ([Pediatrics 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39342414/))

## FAQ

Use 4 steps: find the expression (what are they feeling right now), say the reason (why do they feel that way), try a different way to say it (if it were you, how would you say it), and think of a solution (what can they do to feel better). These 4 steps correspond to the four abilities in the Ministry of Education's Preschool Curriculum Framework emotions domain: awareness and identification, understanding, expression, and regulation. Q2: What emotional abilities are covered in the preschool curriculum? The Ministry of Education's Preschool Curriculum Framework divides emotional abilities into four categories: emotional awareness and identification, emotional expression, emotional understanding, and emotional regulation, divided into the two learning dimensions of "self" and "others and environment." Q3: Does a child need to skip pages with angry or scared content? There is no special need to skip them. The framework notes that both positive and negative emotions have reasons for appearing and are worth exploring; what young children need to learn is to accept their emotions rather than deny them. When reading such content, you can pause and ask the child why the character feels that way. Q4: Is there a custom picture book with an emotions theme where the child is the main character? Yes. Tale With You's "Feelings Planet" theme is [Child's name]'s Feelings Planet, with each planet home to one kind of feeling, and the main character illustrated based on the child's photos. # Fine-Tuning or RAG: How Should a Company Choose? | Q&A Library | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Local LLM
TB24

# Fine-Tuning or RAG: How Should a Company Choose?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-11-06
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/fine-tuning-vs-rag/)

The short answer

Fine-tuning continues training an existing model on task or domain data. RAG retrieves external material at answer time. For current company documents, assess retrieval first; for a stable response pattern or task behavior, test prompting before considering fine-tuning. They can work together, but diagnose the failure first.

## 1. Distinguish training from supplying evidence

Hugging Face defines fine-tuning as continuing training on a smaller, specific dataset. The original RAG research combines model parameters with retrievable external memory. Here, RAG refers to enterprise retrieval at answer time, without requiring every detail of the research architecture.

Dimension
Fine-tuning
Answer-time RAG
Intervention
Train model parameters
Retrieve material for the answer context

Preparation
Approved examples and evaluation tasks
Searchable files, versions, and permissions

Suggested checks
Desired behavior and possible regressions
Correct, authorized supporting evidence

This is a planning comparison, not a performance ranking. “Understand our company” needs a more precise definition: is the model missing a current policy, or ignoring the requested format?

## 2. Let failure examples guide the next step

We suggest testing a small document collection when the need is to consult current policies. Require inspectable references. If all information is present but required fields are missing, try explicit formatting instructions and examples before assessing training data for fine-tuning. This is a suggested sequence, not a universal rule.

Do not treat a fine-tuned model as a document database with individual records that can be inspected and edited. Traceability, document removal, and departmental permissions should be independently implemented and tested. With a combined approach, record both document and model versions.

## 3. Establish a baseline before training

Hugging Face’s tutorial separates training and test data. A company can apply that principle by holding back work questions and comparing the base model, prompt changes, RAG, and fine-tuning. Check correctness, format, appropriate abstention, and evidence rather than a few demonstration answers.

Confirm data rights for either method. Map training-data destinations and custody of model files separately from the destinations of retrieved passages. Local and cloud processing are deployment options subject to approved data boundaries.

Brand information | Think BIG

## Data boundaries and evidence-based verification at Think BIG

Think BIG helps companies deploy AI Agents in their own environments. Running on company hardware does not keep every connection local: cloud models, messaging platforms, and other external services can still receive requests.

- Map data flows first : Before deployment, identify data sources, processing locations, output recipients, logs, and backups. Assess deployment location and external connections separately.

- Verify work with evidence : Completion criteria require corresponding change records and verification results, with maintenance and handover responsibilities defined.

See [Trust](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/) and [Local AI and data sovereignty](https://thinkbigtw.com/guides/local-ai-data/).

The actual scope of Think BIG’s services follows what both parties confirm.

## FAQ

Q1: Must a model be fine-tuned to read new announcements? Assess retrieval and document updates first. Whether training also helps depends on evaluation. Q2: Can RAG and fine-tuning work together? Yes. They address evidence retrieval and model behavior, with end-to-end evaluation still needed. Q3: Is more training data always better? This article offers no universal threshold. Check quality, rights, and evaluation coverage first. Q4: Does local deployment remove data permission requirements? No. Confirm sources, permitted uses, access, and custody.

# What Can Grandparents Give That Is Meaningful? Can Grandparents Be Drawn Into a Custom Book? | Think BIG Q&A Library

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Shared Reading & Custom Picture Books
Q27

# What Can Grandparents Give That Is Meaningful? Can Grandparents Be Drawn Into a Custom Book?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-11-06
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/gift-from-grandparents/)

The short answer

To give a grandchild a gift with sentimental value, you can choose a book the child likes and write a paragraph of your own words inside; if choosing a custom picture book, you can also ask first whether you can appear in the book together. Photo rights and ordering eligibility need to be confirmed separately: grandparents willing to appear in the book does not mean they can directly provide the child's photos. Building in time to read together is the gift recommendation in this article.

## 1. First choose a story the child will want to flip through, then write your own words

The American Academy of Pediatrics' [family reading recommendations](https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/gradeschool/school/Pages/10-Tips-to-Help-Your-Child-Fall-in-Love-with-Reading.aspx) mention that friends and family can give books and leave their own message inside. For writing a dedication, you don't need to write like a greeting card; you can record a small thing you've done together, such as "I really like sitting with you by the window watching the rain," and add one thing you'd like to do together next time.

When choosing the topic, you can ask the parents to share a few theme names for the child to pick from, without having the child decide the entire gift arrangement. Grandparents can also talk about what stories they liked when they were young. These are conversation suggestions; they do not treat giving a particular type of book as having an effect on improving family relationships.

## 2. Before appearing in the book together, clarify the three roles

Using Tale With You as an example, the [Privacy Policy](https://talewithyoutw.com/privacy.html) states that only the child's parents or guardians may place orders and upload photos; adults who appear in the book must be adults and give their own consent. Therefore, the gift-giver, the parent placing the order, and the adult in the photos can be different people; just because someone wants to give a gift does not mean the confirmations from the other people can be skipped.

Role Recommended confirmation first Grandparent giving the gift Explain the theme you would like, and whether you are willing to appear in the book; don't send the child's photos yet.

Parent or guardian placing the order Read the photo usage instructions, choose the official channel for sending photos, and consolidate responses to the preview.

Each adult who appears in the book Review the purpose and handling, and be willing before providing their own solo photo.

This is a division of tasks organized based on the brand's publicly available policies. If the grandparents themselves hold guardianship status, they should still follow the provider's verification procedures; if they are only the gift-giver, have the child's parents or guardians lead the photo and order process. Whether other providers accept third-party orders must be asked separately.

## 3. Help the book last, and let the child keep their choices

It is recommended to confirm the name, nickname, and dedication during the preview, and have the adults who appear in the book view their own illustrations together. For anything you would like to adjust, consolidate it and pass it to the parent placing the order. Don't ask the child to say the illustration looks like them, and don't expect a specific reaction when unwrapping the gift; you can put the book away and invite the child to read it together when they are ready.

If you are planning to take a shared-reading photo as a keepsake, first discuss with the parents whether the photos will stay within the family, be shared with relatives, or be shared publicly; this is another thing to confirm. For details about appearing in the book, see [Notes on adults appearing in a custom picture book](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/parents-in-custom-book/); once the gift date is confirmed, check the [production and shipping schedule](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/custom-book-lead-time/).

If the family doesn't live together, you can first schedule a call, have the child decide which page to look at, and have the grandparent read a section or share a memory. This is a suggestion for arranging shared reading; there is no need to record every conversation; when wanting to keep a memory, first explain who will hear the recording and let the participating family members choose whether they want to keep it.

Brand information | Tale With You

## Tale With You's adult appearance process

Tale With You's [ordering process](https://talewithyoutw.com/how-it-works.html) offers an optional adult photo submission: 1–2 adults can be included, with 1–2 photos per adult, each showing only that adult. The child's name can use a nickname.

According to the [Privacy Policy](https://talewithyoutw.com/privacy.html), if another adult such as a grandparent will appear, their own consent must first be obtained and photo usage instructions provided to them. Which pages the adult appears on depends on the story arrangement; the main character is still the child. Photos of the child are deleted by the provider within 3 days of delivery; the third-party retention scope is per the policy description.

Content in this section is taken from the Tale With You website's ordering process and Privacy Policy, verified on 2026-10-26. All characters in books and videos are AI-generated.

## FAQ

Q1: What is a natural way to write the dedication? You can write one small thing you've done together with the child, then add one thing you'd like to say to them; there is no need to write it as a growth requirement. Q2: Can I use a photo of the grandparent from a family group chat? It is recommended to first explain the purpose to the person in the photo and obtain their consent, then confirm whether the photo is suitable, rather than directly forwarding a group chat photo. Q3: Does the grandparent need to appear in the book? No. You can just write a dedication, choose a theme together, or arrange shared reading time; the gifting approach is left for the family to choose. Q4: Can a grandparent directly upload the child's photos for a Tale With You order? According to the brand's Privacy Policy, only the child's parents or guardians may place orders and upload photos; general gift-givers should have the parents lead the order.

Q25

# How to Choose a Custom Picture Book: 7 Questions to Ask Before You Buy

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-11-04
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/how-to-choose-custom-book/)

The short answer

When choosing a custom picture book, first ask clearly about 7 things: customization scope, story content, physical book specifications, photo use, preview and revisions, delivery schedule, and cancellation and defect handling. Keep the answers and then decide whether to provide photos and place the order. Sample images help you assess the art style; your own preview is what you use to confirm the name and illustrations.

## 1. Turn a page you like into specific questions

It is recommended to first pick one sample page you like and ask the provider "which parts will change in the actual book and which won't." The placement of the name, how the character is illustrated, and whether the story can be adjusted can all be asked separately. Rather than writing "I want it to look a lot like the photo," you can also describe what you care about—the fringe, glasses, or nickname—and ask the provider what range they can handle.

Then paste the following checklist into your own notes app. Leave one line to fill in the answer for each item; when the answer is unclear, stay in the inquiry phase. This is an organization method for making a purchase, not a quality rating of any provider, nor does it judge which type of book is more suitable for a child based on the number of customizable items.

## 2. Ask these 7 questions before ordering

- How much can be customized?  Only the name, or is the character illustrated based on photos? Can a nickname be used? Can adults appear?

- What is the story about?  Which samples can be viewed? Is the plot fixed or adjustable? First see whether the child is interested in the subject.

- What is the physical book like?  How are the size, interior page count, text, paper material, and binding described? Don't treat the art style name as the paper material specification.

- Who gets the photos and where are they used?  Which services are involved in production? Is cross-border processing involved? How long until deletion, and which records cannot be deleted?

- How much of the preview can be seen and what can be revised?  Only the cover or some interior pages? What are the rules for text revisions and regeneration? Can changes still be made after confirmation?

- When is production, when does it arrive?  What is the starting condition—payment, photos submitted, or preview confirmed? Do working days include holidays? How long does shipping take after production?

- What happens with cancellations or defects?  Is the handling different before and after printing? Who do you contact with issues, and what photos or records are needed?

For item 4, the photo notification can be checked against Personal Data Protection Act Article 8, which covers: the name of the collecting party, the purpose of collection, the category of data, the period, territory, recipients, and methods of use, and how the data subject can exercise their rights. ([Laws and Regulations Database](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=I0050021)) The checklist breaks some items into everyday phrasing, which does not mean every question is a legal requirement listed item by item.

## 3. Review the terms, then provide photos and confirm the preview

The Regulations Governing Reasonable Exceptions to the Right of Rescission in Distance Transactions Article 2(2) lists "customized products made at the consumer's request," and Article 2 requires the business to notify the consumer before excluding the right of rescission described in that article. ([Laws and Regulations Database](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=J0170012)) Don't skip reading the cancellation rules just because you see the word "custom." This is provided for reference and does not constitute legal advice.

It is recommended to keep the product description, customer service replies, and the preview you confirmed in the same folder. If you don't know what to ask about the photos, read [photo privacy for custom picture books](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/photo-privacy-custom-book/); for cancellation questions see [returns and exceptions for custom picture books](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/custom-book-return-policy/). Read the name and dedication once more before confirming; there is no need to reply immediately.

Brand information | Tale With You

## Checking the ordering process against the Tale With You checklist

Tale With You's [ordering instructions](https://talewithyoutw.com/order.html) state: the website currently does not accept orders or photos; please order on Shopee; after payment, photo usage instructions are confirmed in Shopee chat, and photos are submitted only after agreement. You can first browse themes and samples on the website.

The [Terms of Service](https://talewithyoutw.com/terms.html) further state that the preview consists of the cover and some interior pages, in low resolution with a watermark; text revisions for name and dedication are unlimited before confirmation; each order may regenerate the entire book once at no charge; once confirmation is replied, printing begins and content cannot be changed. Paper material and binding are per the actual specifications of the printing partner, described on the product page and at preview confirmation.

Content in this section is taken from the Tale With You website's ordering instructions and Terms of Service, verified on 2026-10-26. All characters in books and videos are AI-generated.

## FAQ

Q1: What should I look at first with a custom picture book? First look at the story and samples, then ask which content can be customized and which is fixed, then check the photo use and confirmation process. Q2: Are the sample images the same as my own preview? These two should be confirmed separately. Samples are for assessing the art style; the preview is for confirming the name and character illustration in your own order. Q3: Does a custom product mean defects can't be reported? The right of rescission exception and defect handling are different questions; each should be asked about before purchase; individual disputes need to be judged based on applicable regulations and transaction content. Q4: Where do I order Tale With You? According to the official ordering instructions, orders are currently placed on Shopee; the website itself does not accept orders or photos.
