# Is a Local LLM Smart Enough for Enterprise Use? | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Local LLMs
TB06

# Is a Local LLM Smart Enough, and How Do You Tell Whether It Works for Your Company?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-19
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/is-local-llm-good-enough/)

The short answer

Public leaderboards cannot answer this; test with your own questions. Prepare 30 to 50 questions employees really ask, each with a correct answer, and run the local model and a cloud model on the same company documents, comparing accuracy and speed question by question. Rule out configuration problems before testing: Ollama's default context is only 4,096 tokens, and when retrieved passages do not fit, the model looks "dumb".

## 1. Why leaderboards are not enough

Leaderboards measure general ability. Your company needs answers from your documents, in your language, to your questions. OpenAI's evaluation best practices say the same: design task-specific evals that reflect real-world usage. Anti-patterns it lists include relying only on generic academic metrics, test data that does not match production traffic, and treating "it seems to work" as a pass.

So the question is not "which model is stronger" but "on our 50 questions, how many does it get right, where does it fail, and what does each failure cost?"

## 2. Three configuration reasons a local model seems "dumb"

Before concluding anything, rule out problems unrelated to model ability:

- Context too short for the documents.  Ollama's default context is 4,096 tokens. When AI searches company documents, retrieved passages go into the context; what does not fit is cut off, and the model answers from incomplete material. Raise it with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH  or num_ctx , at the cost of more memory (see "What hardware does a local LLM need?").

- Model not fully on the GPU.  If the PROCESSOR column in ollama ps  shows a CPU/GPU split, part of the model runs on the CPU and responses slow down noticeably. That is a speed problem, not an intelligence problem, but it is often mistaken for "local models don't work".

- Reasoning settings left at default.  Some models let you set reasoning effort; OpenAI's gpt-oss accepts low, medium, or high in the system prompt. Testing multi-step questions at low effort is not a fair test.

## 3. A five-step comparison test

- Collect questions.  Pick 30 to 50 from what employees actually ask, customer service logs, and internal email. Include three kinds: answerable from the documents; not in the documents, where the AI should say it doesn't know or hand off; and questions the user has no permission to see.

- Write correct answers and sources.  For each question, record the answer and which passage of which document it comes from.

- Run both under the same conditions.  Same documents, same retrieval settings, same questions for the local and cloud models.

- Score question by question.  Use four categories (correct, partly correct, wrong, answered when it should have declined) and record response time. Where it fails matters more than the total.

- Set the threshold in advance.  For example, a required share of correct answers on answerable questions, and zero made-up answers on questions that should be declined. Adopt only if met. When you change models or settings later, rerun the same set.

The usual outcome is not "all local" or "all cloud" but a split: which work goes to the local model, and which work, where the data allows, uses the cloud-assisted version.

Brand information | Think BIG

## How Think BIG decides whether a model is good enough

Think BIG (Think BIG Make it Real CO., LTD.) is an enterprise AI Agent deployment provider headquartered in Taiwan. Starting from protecting company data, we build AI Agents inside the client's own environment (company hardware, or a cloud server under the company's account). There are two deployment options: with the on-premises version, models and documents are processed on company hardware; with the cloud-assisted version, employees' questions and the document passages the system retrieves are sent to the model provider for processing.

- Acceptance by test questions, not demos : people who know the business write test questions, correct sources, and acceptable answer ranges; each retrieved passage and final answer is checked, including cases the AI cannot answer and permission boundaries.

- Re-verify after changing models : when a model is changed, the workflow and output quality are re-verified, and whether existing settings still apply is decided by test results.

- Pre-delivery security review : before each system is delivered, its code and configuration go through a security review; if it does not pass, it is not delivered.

## FAQ

Q1: How far behind cloud models like ChatGPT are local models? It depends on the task; public leaderboards cannot answer it for your company. Run 30 to 50 real company questions on both, with the same documents and settings, and compare accuracy and speed question by question. Q2: Why does a local model answer poorly when reading company documents? Often the context is too short. Ollama's default context is 4,096 tokens, so retrieved passages that do not fit are cut off. You can raise the context, but memory use goes up. Q3: How many questions are needed to test a local model? About 30 to 50, covering questions answerable from documents, questions the AI should decline or hand off, and questions the user has no permission to see, each with a correct answer and source. Q4: After switching to a new local model, do we need to test again? Yes. After any model or setting change, rerun the same test set and confirm accuracy and declining behavior have not regressed before going live.

# Choosing a Language-Learning App for Your Child: 5 Things to Check Before Downloading | Q&A Library | Think BIG

# Choosing a Language-Learning App for Your Child: 5 Things to Check Before Downloading

Think BIG Q&A Library　·　November 9, 2026 　·　[中文版](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/kids-learning-app-privacy-checklist/)

Short answer

Before downloading a language-learning app for a child, check five things: what data it collects from the child, whether parental consent is needed, who receives the data, how long it is kept, and how to request deletion. The US COPPA Rule covers online services directed to children under 13 and requires notice to parents and verifiable parental consent before personal information is collected, and retention only as long as necessary for the purpose. In Taiwan, Article 8 of the Personal Data Protection Act requires businesses to disclose the period, area, recipients and manner of use, and Article 3 protects the right to inquire and request deletion.

## 1. Why check at all

Children's learning apps often need a child's name, voice or usage records. The US Federal Trade Commission explains that the COPPA Rule is designed to put parents in control of what information is collected from their young children online, and that it applies to websites and apps (including mobile apps) directed to children under 13 that collect, use or disclose their personal information. ([FTC: COPPA FAQ](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/complying-coppa-frequently-asked-questions)) The FTC page notes the Rule was amended on 22 April 2025, so check the amended Rule for the exact requirements.

## 2. Five checks before downloading

Check What to look for Basis
1. What data is collected Does the privacy policy list specific items (name, voice, usage records, device information), not vague wording such as "necessary data"? PDPA Art. 8: collectors must disclose purpose and categories of data

2. Is parental consent needed For services directed to under-13s, is there a parental-consent step, rather than the child simply tapping "agree"? COPPA: notice to parents and verifiable parental consent

3. Who receives the data Does it mention cloud, voice or analytics providers? Is data processed outside Taiwan? PDPA Art. 8: disclose the period, area, recipients and manner of use

4. How long it is kept Is there a concrete retention period rather than "indefinitely"? COPPA: keep only as long as necessary and delete with reasonable measures

5. How to request deletion Is there a clear contact channel and response time? PDPA Art. 3: rights to inquire, review, correct, stop use and request deletion, which cannot be waived in advance

The text of Taiwan's PDPA is at the [Laws and Regulations Database (Chinese)](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=I0050021).

## 3. What parents can do

1. Read the store disclosures first.  If a privacy policy link is missing or vague, do not download yet.

2. Do not register with a child's real name or photo.  Use a nickname where possible, and do not upload photos if the service does not need them.

3. Review and delete regularly.  When you stop using it, request deletion under the policy and remove the app.

4. Use it together.  Using the app with your child and talking about it gives more control than leaving it to the child.

# No Tech Background and Official AI Courses Feel Hard to Follow: How Do You Start Learning to Use AI?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-11-02
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/learn-ai-without-tech-background/)

The short answer

Start by using a free chat AI to finish one small everyday task, then go back to the official course once you have a feel for it; you do not have to finish a whole course first. Official courses from AI companies are thorough, and some say beginners are welcome, but the pages are mostly in English and use terms such as prompts, models, and workflows, so if you get stuck halfway, try the task first and come back. Three habits: learn one thing at a time, use everyday examples, and use free tools . If you want someone to walk you through it step by step, watch Think BIG Academy's "Keeping Up with AI" series (陪你跟上 AI, in Mandarin): BIG explains one topic per episode in 1 to 2 minutes. Start with Episode 1, "I know nothing about AI. Is it too late to start?"

## 1. What the official courses teach

These are public learning resources from several AI companies (see the official pages for current details):

Course
Provider
How the official page describes it

Anthropic

These are all good resources. For someone who has never used AI, the usual sticking point is not the course itself but that, without having tried AI, it is hard to picture what the course is describing. Try it yourself a few times first, and many ideas in the course will click.

## 2. Three habits for complete beginners

- Learn one thing at a time.  Today, learn only how to ask AI to turn your to-do list into three tasks. You do not need models, prompts, and Agents all at once.

- Use everyday examples.  Start with things you do daily: sorting a to-do list, drafting a message to a friend, asking what to cook with what is left in the fridge. The closer to daily life, the easier to remember.

- Use free tools.  Many chat AIs have a free plan; for example, Claude has a Free plan for chatting on the web, desktop, and mobile. Practice on a free plan first, and consider other plans only once you know you will use it.

## 3. A 5-step beginner path

- Pick a free chat AI and sign in.  The phone or computer you already have is enough; no new device needed.

- In week one, do just one small everyday task.  For example, paste in your to-do list and ask it to "turn this into three things I can finish today, and ask me how much time I have first."

- State what you want clearly, and keep refining.  Say who it is for, the goal, and any limits. If the answer is too long, say "cut it to three lines"; if it is too hard, say "explain it so a middle schooler would understand."

- Build a habit of checking.  AI can be wrong while sounding confident (see [When AI is wrong but sounds confident](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/news/ai-hallucination-20261012/)). Double-check numbers and anything about health, law, or money, and do not paste in ID numbers, passwords, or other people's personal data.

- Once you have a feel for it, return to the official courses.  AI Fluency, OpenAI Academy, or Google AI Essentials will then connect more easily with your own experience.

# Can Children Learn Mandarin from Videos? What the Research Says and How to Use Them | Q&A Library | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

熊好學 · BearSay Mandarin BS04

# Can Children Learn Mandarin from Videos? What the Research Says and How to Use Them

Think BIG Q&A Library　·　November 9, 2026 　·　[中文版](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/learn-language-from-video/)

Short answer

Children can learn from video, but the effect depends on age and on whether a real person interacts with them. In Kuhl and colleagues' 2003 experiment, 9-month-old infants who heard live Mandarin speakers kept the ability to tell Mandarin sounds apart, while those who saw the same material only on recordings did not. Roseberry and colleagues (2009) studied 96 children aged 30 to 42 months and found that younger children learned verbs from video only with live social interaction, while older children could learn from video alone. Video works best as a supplement, with a parent watching along and talking about it.

## 1. Two studies

Study Method Result
Kuhl, Tsao & Liu (2003)
PNAS 9-month-old American infants in 12 lab sessions with live native Mandarin speakers; other groups got the same material by audiovisual or audio-only recording. The live group kept the ability to discriminate Mandarin sounds; the recorded groups showed no effect.

Roseberry, Hirsh-Pasek, Parish-Morris & Golinkoff (2009)
Child Development 96 children aged 30 to 42 months learning verbs with live interaction, video alone, or a person shown on screen. Younger children needed live interaction to learn verbs; older children could learn from video alone.

Sources: [Kuhl et al., 2003](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1532872100); [Roseberry et al., 2009](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-8624.2009.01338.x).

## 2. How to read them

Age matters.  The younger the child, the more they need someone responding. For somewhat older children, video helps more.

They measured specific skills.  One measured infants' sound discrimination and the other verb learning. Neither equals overall Mandarin ability.

Screen time still has limits.  The World Health Organization's 2019 guidelines say screen time is not recommended for infants under 1 or for 1-year-olds, and that for ages 2 and above sedentary screen time should be no more than 1 hour a day, with less being better. ([WHO, 2019](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241550536)) More in [screen time under 5 (Chinese)](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/screen-time-under-5/).

## 3. How parents can combine them

1. Watch together.  Point, pause and ask "What was that?"

2. Use it the same day.  Use the word from the video once at home so the child gets to say it.

3. Choose short over long.  A few minutes is easier to follow with conversation than a long stretch of playback.

4. Do not replace the speakers.  People who can speak Mandarin with the child remain the most important resource.

Brand information | BearSay Mandarin

## Where BearSay Mandarin's videos fit

BearSay Mandarin (熊好學) is a learning brand for Taiwan Mandarin. Every day it teaches one Taiwan Mandarin word on Instagram ([@bearsaymandarin](https://www.instagram.com/bearsaymandarin/)), in Traditional characters with zhuyin and pinyin and multilingual subtitles, guided by five characters: BUBU, MIBO, HUBO, GUIBO and LANBO. The app is in development and has not been released. Release information will appear on the [BearSay Mandarin Q&A overview](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/bearsay/).

BearSay Mandarin currently publishes short videos and carousel posts. Based on the research above, this kind of content works best as a starting point for watching together and then talking. It does not replace real conversation and does not guarantee any learning result.

Source: the public Instagram account and this site's brand overview, updated 2026-11-09. Demo audio is AI-synthesized speech; BearSay Mandarin characters are AI-generated.

## Frequently asked questions

Q1: Can children learn Mandarin from videos? To some extent, depending on age and interaction. In Kuhl et al. (2003) infants kept Mandarin sound discrimination after live exposure but not recordings. Roseberry et al. (2009) found younger toddlers learned verbs only with live interaction, while older ones could learn from video alone. Q2: Can toddlers learn to speak from video alone? Both studies show younger children need live interaction more. They measured sound discrimination and verb learning, so they cannot be generalised to overall language ability. Q3: How much screen time is suitable? WHO 2019: not recommended under 1, not recommended at 1, and no more than 1 hour of sedentary screen time a day from age 2, with less being better. Q4: How should parents use video? Watch along and talk, use the video's word at home the same day, choose short clips, and keep time for talking with real people.

Sources (links checked 2026-11-09)

- Kuhl, Tsao & Liu (2003). Foreign-language experience in infancy: Effects of short-term exposure and social interaction on phonetic learning. PNAS, 100(15), 9096–9101: [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1532872100)

- Roseberry, Hirsh-Pasek, Parish-Morris & Golinkoff (2009). Live action: Can young children learn verbs from video? Child Development, 80(5), 1360–1375: [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-8624.2009.01338.x)

- World Health Organization (2019). Guidelines on physical activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep for children under 5 years of age: [www.who.int](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241550536)

# Local LLM Advantages: 5 Benefits for Enterprise | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Local LLMs
TB13

# What Are the Advantages of a Local LLM? Five Benefits of Running AI Inside the Company

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-26
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/local-llm-advantages/)

The short answer

The biggest advantage of a local LLM is that the company decides where its data goes: the model runs on company hardware, so questions, documents, and answers are processed inside the company instead of being sent to an outside model provider. There are four more benefits: it works offline, the company decides when to change model versions, usage logs stay in the company's hands, and use can be separated by confidentiality level. Each benefit has conditions, though: outbound connections must be turned off, someone must maintain the system, and the drawbacks must be weighed too.

## 1. Five benefits

Benefit
Why
Condition
1. Data does not have to leave the company
The official FAQ of a common local-model tool states that when you run locally, its developer does not see your prompts or data; only when you use its cloud models are prompts and responses sent to its service. With hardware in Taiwan, data can also stay in Taiwan; Article 21 of Taiwan's Personal Data Protection Act lets the authority restrict a non-government entity's international transfer of personal data in cases such as major national interests or inadequate data protection laws in the receiving country.
Turn off the tool's cloud features; check external channels such as LINE or email one by one, because messages through them still leave the company; include backup, monitoring, and update services located abroad.

2. Works offline
Once a model is downloaded to the machine, inference needs no network, so it can run in an environment with no outside connection.
Updates are downloaded and verified on a connected machine first, then moved in. See [Can a local LLM work offline?](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/offline-local-llm-updates/)

3. The company decides the version
The model files sit on company hardware, so the company decides when to change versions and can verify a new one with its own test questions first.
Some local tools' desktop apps download software updates automatically; switch to manual updates and pinned versions.

4. Logs stay in the company
Who asked what and which documents the AI read are stored on company hardware. Article 12 of the Enforcement Rules of Taiwan's Personal Data Protection Act lists "usage records, trail data and preservation of evidence" as one of the security measures that may be adopted.
Logs contain personal data too, so set access rights and retention periods.

5. Use by confidentiality level
Confidential and personal data can be processed on-premises while general work uses the cloud. Point 4 of the reference guidelines for the Executive Yuan treats closed, on-premises deployment as an option for use "according to confidentiality level" (see the next section).
Set data classification rules first, and confirm the on-premises environment is secure.

## 2. How Taiwan's public sector views "on-premises"

The Reference Guidelines for the Use of Generative AI by the Executive Yuan and Its Agencies, drafted by the National Science and Technology Council, reported to the Executive Yuan Council on August 31, 2023, and issued to agencies for reference, say in point 4 that staff must not give generative AI information that must be kept confidential, personal information, or information not approved for release. However, a closed, on-premises generative AI model may be used according to confidentiality level after the security of the system environment has been confirmed .

These guidelines bind government agencies, not private companies. But they make one point clear: for confidential data, "sent outside for processing" and "processed in your own environment" are treated as two different situations. And even on-premises, the environment must be confirmed secure first; installing it is not enough.

## 3. Three things that must be true first

- Confirm nothing is going out.  On-premises does not mean every connection stays local; cloud models, messaging platforms, and external services all send requests out. For where data goes step by step, see [When AI searches company documents, where does the data go?](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/rag-data-flow-cloud-vs-local/)

- Someone is responsible for maintenance.  NIST SP 800-40 Rev. 4 frames patching as preventive maintenance, a necessary, ongoing part of using technology. Local models, operating systems, and surrounding software all need updates.

- The hardware can run it.  Without enough GPU memory, the model runs slowly or a smaller model must be used. See [What hardware does a company need to run a local LLM?](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/local-llm-hardware-sizing/)

Local LLMs also have drawbacks: upfront hardware cost, capability that usually trails the latest cloud models, and the need for maintenance. Whether one fits should be decided by weighing the benefits and drawbacks together.

Brand information | Think BIG

## Think BIG's two deployment options

Think BIG (Think BIG Make it Real CO., LTD.) is an enterprise AI Agent deployment provider headquartered in Taiwan. Starting from protecting company data, we build AI Agents inside the client's own environment (company hardware, or a cloud server under the company's account). There are two deployment options: with the on-premises version, models and documents are processed on company hardware; with the cloud-assisted version, employees' questions and the document passages the system retrieves are sent to the model provider for processing.

- Data flow listed before building : where the application, model, knowledge-base index, source documents, logs, and backups each sit is listed item by item.

- External channels confirmed one by one : on-premises does not mean every connection stays local. If an external channel such as LINE is added, messages through that channel pass through that service; we list this for the client before building.

- Pinned versions, no automatic updates : third-party packages are reviewed for source and license, pinned, and not auto-updated. Each system goes through a security review before delivery; if it does not pass, it is not delivered.

See [On-premises AI and data sovereignty](https://thinkbigtw.com/guides/local-ai-data/) and [Trust](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/).

The actual scope of Think BIG's services follows what both parties confirm.

## FAQ

Q1: What are the advantages of a local LLM? The biggest advantage is that the company decides where its data goes: questions, documents, and answers are processed on company hardware. It also works offline, the company decides when to change model versions, usage logs stay in-house, and use can be separated by confidentiality level. Q2: Does a local LLM mean data can never leak? No. On-premises does not mean every connection stays local. If the tool's cloud features are on, or messages pass through external channels such as LINE or email, that content still leaves. Check outbound connections one by one and set permissions and logging. Q3: Can Taiwan government agencies use a local LLM for confidential work? Point 4 of the National Science and Technology Council's reference guidelines for the Executive Yuan says staff must not give generative AI confidential, personal, or unreleased information, but a closed, on-premises generative AI model may be used according to confidentiality level after the security of the system environment has been confirmed. Q4: Can a local LLM run fully offline? Yes. Once the model is downloaded, inference needs no network. Turn off the tool's cloud features, and download and verify updates on a connected machine before moving them into the offline environment.

Sources (checked 2026-10-24)

# Local LLM Hardware: GPU Memory Guide | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Local LLMs
TB02

# What Hardware Does a Company Need to Run a Local LLM, and How Much GPU Memory?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-19
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/local-llm-hardware-sizing/)

The short answer

Start with GPU memory, not the CPU. The model file must fit entirely in GPU memory, with room left for context and the number of people using it at once. Going by download sizes in Ollama's official library, an 8B-class model is about 5.2GB, 14B about 9.3GB, and 32B about 20GB. OpenAI states that gpt-oss-20b can run within 16GB of memory, while gpt-oss-120b fits on a single 80GB GPU.

## 1. Why GPU memory comes first

To answer a question, a local model has to be loaded into memory. Whatever fits in GPU memory runs on the GPU; whatever does not is placed in system memory and computed by the CPU, which is noticeably slower.

Ollama's ollama ps  shows the split directly. A PROCESSOR value of 100% GPU  means the whole model is on the graphics card; a ratio such as 48%/52% CPU/GPU  means only part of it fits (the example in Ollama's FAQ). So the order is: decide the model size, check whether GPU memory is enough, then look at everything else.

## 2. How much space common models need

Download sizes from Ollama's official library (default tags, checked 2026-10-19). File size roughly equals the memory needed to load the model; context needs additional memory on top.

Model

Hardware reference points (official figures):

- Consumer graphics card example: the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 has 32GB of GDDR7 memory, enough for every model above up to 32B.

- Desktop AI system example: NVIDIA DGX Spark has 128GB of unified memory; NVIDIA states a single unit runs models up to 200 billion parameters.

Prices and availability in Taiwan change quickly, so this page lists none; check current quotes from resellers.

## 3. Four steps to choose hardware

1. Decide the task, then the model.  Answering from company documents, organizing data, and drafting replies usually work with mid-sized models. There is no need to start with a machine for the largest model. To judge whether a model is good enough, see "Is a local model smart enough?"

2. Size GPU memory from the model file, with headroom.  Ollama's default context is 4,096 tokens. Letting the AI read more document passages at once means raising the context, which uses more memory.

3. Count concurrent users separately.  Ollama's FAQ states that OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL  sets how many requests each model handles at once, and required memory scales with parallel requests times context length. When memory runs short, new requests queue. Ten people asking at once need more memory than one.

4. Place and configure the machine properly.  An AI Agent that must respond at any time needs a machine that stays on 24 hours. Ollama binds to 127.0.0.1 port 11434 by default; if you open it to the office network, use a firewall to allow only specific devices, and do not expose it to the internet.

## FAQ

Q1: For a local LLM, does the CPU or the graphics card matter more? Start with GPU memory. When the whole model fits, the GPU does the work; whatever does not fit goes to the CPU and slows things down noticeably. With Ollama, the PROCESSOR column in `ollama ps` shows the split. Q2: What can run on 16GB of GPU memory? By Ollama's official library sizes, 8B-class (about 5.2GB) and 14B-class (about 9.3GB) models fit. OpenAI also states that gpt-oss-20b runs within 16GB of memory. Leave room for context. Q3: How much memory if many staff use it at once? Calculate it separately. Ollama's FAQ states that required memory scales with the number of parallel requests times context length, and new requests queue when memory runs short. To let other office devices use it, open access to specific devices through a firewall rather than to the internet.

# Local LLM Limitations & When Cloud AI Is Better | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Local LLMs
TB14

# What Are the Drawbacks of a Local LLM, and When Is the Cloud the Better Choice?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-27
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/local-llm-limitations/)

The short answer

Local LLMs have five drawbacks to face honestly: hardware must be bought upfront; capability usually trails the latest cloud models, because the models company hardware can run are usually smaller than the largest ones; someone must maintain, update, and monitor the system; and when usage is low or uneven, the hardware sits idle and the cost is hard to justify; and power, cooling, floor space, hardware depreciation and replacement, and backup and disaster recovery all become the company's responsibility. Running on-premises also does not automatically solve prompt injection or permission settings. So when data may leave the company, usage is small, the newest capabilities are needed, or no one can maintain the system, the cloud is often the better fit; a common approach is to mix both according to data classification.

## 1. Five drawbacks

Drawback
Why
How to reduce it
1. Upfront hardware cost
A model runs well only if it fits entirely in GPU memory, and larger models need more expensive hardware. With the cloud, you pay for what you use and buy no hardware upfront.
Start with one workflow and size the hardware from actual usage. See [What hardware does a company need to run a local LLM?](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/local-llm-hardware-sizing/)

2. A capability gap
Stanford's AI Index 2025 reports that the gap between open-weight and closed models on some benchmarks shrank from 8% to 1.7% in one year (2024 data). The gap is narrowing, but company hardware usually cannot run the largest open models.
Test with the company's own questions, not leaderboards. See [Is a local LLM smart enough?](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/is-local-llm-good-enough/)

3. Someone must maintain it
NIST SP 800-40 Rev. 4 frames patching as preventive maintenance and a regular cost of using technology. Local models, operating systems, drivers, and surrounding packages all need someone to update, monitor, and back them up.
Decide upfront who is responsible and how often checks happen; pin versions and test before updating.

4. Poor value at low or uneven usage
Hardware capacity is fixed: when usage is low, the hardware sits idle; at peak times, many users at once slow responses down.
Estimate normal and peak usage first, then choose on-premises, cloud, or a mix.

5. Asset responsibilities return to the company
Hardware needs power, cooling, and space; it depreciates and must be replaced after some years; and backup and disaster recovery (restoring after a hardware failure or facility incident) become the company's job rather than a cloud provider's.
Plan power and cooling, a replacement schedule, backup locations, and restore drills before deployment.

Points 4 and 5 are practical judgments, not conclusions of the sources above.

## 2. On-premises does not make it secure by itself

Putting the model inside the company answers "does the data leave?" Many of the risks in OWASP's 2025 Top 10 for LLM applications have nothing to do with where the model runs. Prompt injection (LLM01): if a document or web page the AI reads hides instructions, a local model is affected too. Excessive agency (LLM06): if an AI Agent has too much permission, a local deployment can fail the same way. These are handled with permission design, human approval, and testing. See [What is prompt injection?](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/prompt-injection-ai-agent/) and [How should AI Agent permissions be set?](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/ai-agent-permissions/)

## 3. When the cloud is the better fit

These are practical judgments:

- The data may leave the company.  The work involves public data or marketing copy with no personal or confidential information.

- Usage is small or still a trial.  If you do not yet know whether it will be used daily, trying it in the cloud first is safer than buying hardware.

- The newest capabilities are needed.  The work needs capabilities only the latest cloud models provide, and local models tested with your own questions really fall short.

- No one can maintain it.  If no staff member or vendor is responsible for updates and monitoring, unattended local hardware can be riskier.

- Demand is very uneven.  Large volumes arrive occasionally, with almost no use in between.

## 4. Mixing both by data classification

A common approach is not to choose one or the other but to classify data: confidential and personal data go on-premises, general work goes to the cloud. Point 4 of the National Science and Technology Council's reference guidelines for the Executive Yuan follows similar logic: confidential and personal information must not normally be given to generative AI, while closed, on-premises deployments may be used by confidentiality level after the environment is confirmed secure. For how to classify, see [What are the risks when employees paste company data into ChatGPT?](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/employees-chatgpt-company-data/); for the benefits of local LLMs, see [What are the advantages of a local LLM?](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/local-llm-advantages/)

Brand information | Think BIG

## FAQ

Q1: What are the drawbacks of a local LLM? There are five main ones: upfront hardware cost; capability that usually trails the latest cloud models; the need for someone to maintain, update, and monitor it; poor value when usage is low or uneven, because hardware capacity is fixed; and responsibility for power, cooling, space, hardware replacement, and backup and disaster recovery returning to the company. Running on-premises also does not automatically solve prompt injection or permission problems. Q2: How far behind cloud models are local models? It depends on the task. Stanford's AI Index 2025 reports that the gap between open-weight and closed models on some benchmarks shrank from 8% to 1.7% in one year (2024 data), but company hardware usually cannot run the largest models, so test with the company's own questions to see the real gap. Q3: When is the cloud the better choice? Usually when the data may leave the company, usage is small or still a trial, the newest capabilities are needed and local models tested short, no one can maintain the system, or demand is very uneven. Q4: Can on-premises and cloud be mixed? Yes. A common approach is to classify data: confidential and personal data go on-premises, general work goes to the cloud. Write the classification rules down so employees know which data may be sent to the cloud.

# Will Mixing Mandarin, Taiwanese and English at Home Confuse My Child? | Q&A Library | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

熊好學 · BearSay Mandarin BS08

# Will Mixing Mandarin, Taiwanese and English at Home Confuse My Child?

Think BIG Q&A Library　·　November 9, 2026 　·　[中文版](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/mixing-languages-at-home/)

Short answer

No consistent research says that mixing languages at home always confuses a child. Kaushanskaya and Crespo (2019) studied 174 Spanish-English bilingual children with an average age of 7.8 and found that the effect of hearing code-switching depends on the child's verbal working memory: for children with high working memory, more exposure was linked to higher language ability, and for children with lower working memory, to lower ability. So there is no single answer about whether mixing is good or bad. Families who want to reduce confusion often assign languages to people or situations; that is practical advice, not a finding of this study.

## 1. What the study did

Kaushanskaya and Crespo (2019) recruited 174 Spanish-English bilingual children with a mean age of 7.78, measured their language ability in both languages, collected parent reports of how often the children heard code-switching, and analysed this against each child's verbal working memory. ([Child Development, 2019](https://doi.org/10.1111/cdev.13235))

Child's verbal working memory More exposure to code-switching was linked to
Higher Higher language ability

Lower Lower language ability

## 2. How to read it

An association, not a cause.  The study used parent-reported frequency and did not ask families to change how they speak.

School-aged children.  The average age was 7.8, so it may not apply to toddlers.

Different language pair.  It was Spanish and English, not Mandarin or Taiwanese.

The point is that it depends on the child.  The authors concluded that a child's cognitive processing capacity determines whether code-switching exposure helps or hinders language skills.

## 3. Common household approaches

These are approaches families often use. We found no research showing that any one is best, so adjust to your child:

1. One person, one language.  For example, Mum speaks Mandarin and Grandma speaks Taiwanese.

2. One setting, one language.  For example, Mandarin at meals and another language at bedtime.

3. Do not scold mixing.  Naturally say it back in the language the moment calls for.

4. Make sure each language has enough input.  Performance in each language is related to the proportion heard (see [two languages and speech delay](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/bilingual-children-language-delay/)).

Brand information | BearSay Mandarin

## BearSay Mandarin and multilingual families

BearSay Mandarin (熊好學) is a learning brand for Taiwan Mandarin. Every day it teaches one Taiwan Mandarin word on Instagram ([@bearsaymandarin](https://www.instagram.com/bearsaymandarin/)), in Traditional characters with zhuyin and pinyin and multilingual subtitles, guided by five characters: BUBU, MIBO, HUBO, GUIBO and LANBO. The app is in development and has not been released. Release information will appear on the [BearSay Mandarin Q&A overview](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/bearsay/).

BearSay Mandarin teaches Taiwan Mandarin. In English, "Taiwanese" often means Taiwanese Hokkien, so this site writes Taiwan Mandarin. Multilingual families can treat the daily word as a regular Mandarin touchpoint. There is no guarantee of any learning result.

Source: the public Instagram account and this site's brand overview, updated 2026-11-09. Demo audio is AI-synthesized speech; BearSay Mandarin characters are AI-generated.

## Frequently asked questions

Q1: Will mixing Mandarin, Taiwanese and English confuse my child? No consistent research says it always does. Kaushanskaya and Crespo (2019) studied 174 bilingual children averaging 7.8 years and found the effect depends on the child's verbal working memory. Q2: Is language mixing good or bad for children? There is no single answer. In that study children with higher working memory did better with more exposure, and children with lower working memory did worse. It is an association, not a cause. Q3: How can I reduce the chance of confusion? Families often assign languages to people or situations and make sure each language has enough input. That is practical advice, not a finding of the study. Q4: Should I correct my child for mixing languages? No need to scold. Naturally say it back in the language the moment calls for.

Sources (links checked 2026-11-09)

- Kaushanskaya & Crespo (2019). Does exposure to code-switching influence language performance in bilingual children? Child Development, 90(3), 708–718: [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1111/cdev.13235)

- Hoff et al. (2012). Dual language exposure and early bilingual development. Journal of Child Language, 39(1), 1–27: [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0305000910000759)

# What Difference Does It Make to Put a Child's Name in a Story? | Think BIG Q&A Library

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Shared Reading & Custom Picture Books
Q12

# What Difference Does It Make to Put a Child's Name in a Story?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-22
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/name-in-story-book/)

The short answer

Writing a name into a story is better suited as an opening that grabs a child's attention and makes them feel the story is theirs; there is no research yet proving that "having their name in the book" makes children love reading more or learn better. Research has found that infants as young as about 4.5 months old already prefer to hear the sound of their own name; 5-month-old infants pay more attention to objects they see after hearing their own name, though these are infant responses measured in a laboratory.

## 1. What two studies found

Study Child's age What was done and found
Mandel, Jusczyk & Pisoni (1995)
Psychological Science  6(5), 314–317 About 4.5 months Used a "head-turn preference" experiment to compare infant responses to hearing their own name versus other names (including names with the same stress pattern). Infants showed a clear preference for their own name — meaning they listened to their own name longer than other names. ([Journal page](https://www.psychologicalscience.org/journals/psychological-science/j.1467-9280.1995.tb00517.x/), [University at Buffalo press release](https://www.buffalo.edu/news/releases/1994/06/3135.html))

Parise, Friederici & Striano (2010)
PLoS ONE  5(12), e14208 5 months Measured brain waves and found that infants' brain responses could distinguish their own name from a stranger's name from the very start of the name; after hearing their own name, they also paid more attention to the objects that appeared next. The authors concluded that 5-month-old infants not only recognize their own name but also use it as a social cue that guides their attention. ([PubMed Central full text](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2997051/))

## 2. What these studies did not say

They did not test "name in a book."  Both studies had infants listen to the sound of a name, not read a book. Neither study answers whether having a name in a book title or story makes children more engaged or learn better.

They tested infants.  The subjects were infants about 5 months old; how older children feel when they see their name written in a book cannot be directly inferred from this.

For research on books where the child is the main character and the limitations of that research, see [Do books where the child is the main character really help with reading?](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/personalized-book-research/)

## 3. How parents can use the name during shared reading

Use the name to wake up attention.  When turning to a new page, say the child's name first and then point to the illustration — echoing the research finding that infants pay more attention to what they see next after hearing their own name.

Use the name to bring the child into the story.  When reading about something the main character does, ask "If it were [child's name], what would you do?" and let the child continue in their own words.

Nicknames work too.  Whatever the child normally hears, use that; the name in the book does not need to be the full registered name.

Brand information | Tale With You

For example, the "birthday" theme is titled [Child's name]'s Birthday Adventure , and the "bedtime" theme is titled [Child's name]'s Bedtime Dream Journey . The child's name is entered at step 3 of the ordering process (see "How it works" on the website).

Content in this section is taken from the Tale With You website's FAQ and "How it works" pages, verified on 2026-10-15. All characters in books and videos are AI-generated.

## FAQ

Q1: At what age do infants recognize their own name? Mandel et al.'s 1995 study found that infants around 4.5 months old listened to their own name longer than other names; Parise et al.'s 2010 study found that 5-month-old infants' brain responses could distinguish their own name from a stranger's name. Q2: Does writing a child's name in a book make them love reading more? There is no research that directly proves this. The two studies above measured infant responses to hearing a name, not the effect of having a name in a book. A name is better suited as an opening that grabs attention and makes the child feel the story is theirs. Q3: What happens when an infant hears their own name? Five-month-old infants pay more attention to objects that appear next after hearing their own name. The study authors believed they treat their own name as a social cue that guides their attention. Q4: Where does the child's name appear in a Tale With You book? It appears in the book title and in the story; a nickname can be used. For example, the "birthday" theme is titled [Child's name]'s Birthday Adventure.

Sources (checked 2026-10-15)

- Mandel, D. R., Jusczyk, P. W., & Pisoni, D. B. (1995). Infants’ recognition of the sound patterns of their own names. Psychological Science , 6(5), 314–317 (journal page): [www.psychologicalscience.org](https://www.psychologicalscience.org/journals/psychological-science/j.1467-9280.1995.tb00517.x/)

- University at Buffalo News Release (1994): “Infants as young as 4½ months recognize their name”: [www.buffalo.edu](https://www.buffalo.edu/news/releases/1994/06/3135.html)

# A New Baby Is Coming: How to Prepare an Older Child, and How Picture Books Can Help | Think BIG Q&A Library

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Shared Reading & Custom Picture Books
Q06

# A New Baby Is Coming: How to Prepare an Older Child, and How Picture Books Can Help

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-16
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/new-sibling-preparation/)

The short answer

To help an older child prepare to welcome a new sibling, the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) recommends three things: tell them early in a way they can understand — such as reading together picture books about newborns and becoming a big sibling; aim to complete major changes like potty training or moving from a crib to a bed before the new baby is born, and if that's not possible, wait until after the baby is settled at home; and after the baby arrives, set aside a daily period that belongs only to the older child.

## 1. Before the baby: let the older child prepare gradually

Find a natural moment to tell them.  AAP does not specify a pregnancy week to tell the child; it recommends finding a natural opening, such as when the child starts asking "Why is Mum's tummy getting bigger?" or when you're shopping for baby clothes together. ([AAP HealthyChildren](https://healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/prenatal/Pages/Preparing-Your-Family-for-a-New-Baby.aspx)) The U.S. National Library of Medicine's MedlinePlus also recommends that the child hear the news from you before everyone around them is talking about it. ([MedlinePlus](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/patientinstructions/000635.htm))

Explain time in ways the child can feel.  Toddlers don't yet understand "three months from now." MedlinePlus recommends using something the child can sense, such as "When the weather gets cold, the baby will come." It also suggests not asking the child "Do you want a brother or a sister?" to avoid disappointment.

Read together about newborns and siblings.  AAP recommends reading picture books about newborns and siblings together with toddlers and preschoolers, to help the child become familiar with words like "big sister," "little brother," and "new baby."

Schedule major changes away from the birth.  AAP recommends completing potty training or moving from a crib to a bed before the baby is born if possible; if not, wait until after the baby is settled at home.

## 2. After the baby: the older child needs to feel seen

Expect some regression.  AAP notes the older child may have accidents or want a bottle again. Rather than saying "you're already grown up," praise them when they act like a big kid.

Set aside daily exclusive time.  Reading together, playing, or chatting all count — the key is that this time belongs only to them. When relatives visit to see the baby, also ask them to spend a little time with the older child.

Let them help.  Fetching diapers or singing to the baby gives the older child a sense of being part of the team rather than left out.

Tell them about when they were little.  MedlinePlus mentions that children love hearing their own story: bring out photos from the pregnancy and their infancy, and tell them about things you did together.

## 3. Questions to ask during shared reading with the older child

1.  "When the baby cries, what do you think they want?" 2.  "How could you help?" 3.  "Were you like this when you were little?" (then bring out their baby photos) 4.  "How do you feel right now? Being a bit nervous is fine." Let the older child know that saying "I'm a little nervous" is okay.

Brand information | Tale With You

[Becoming a big sibling](https://talewithyoutw.com/themes/big-sibling.html): [Child's name]'s Big-Sibling Practice . With a new person about to join the family, the child practices holding gently, speaking softly, folding tiny clothes, and also practices saying "I'm a little nervous." By the time they really meet the baby, they're ready.

The main character is illustrated based on the older child's photos, and the child's name appears in the book title and story. Parents can optionally submit their own photos to appear as well. Each book is 21 × 21 cm, 26 interior pages, Chinese with Zhuyin, with English optional.

## FAQ

Q1: When should you tell the older child they're getting a sibling? The American Academy of Pediatrics does not specify a fixed number of weeks; it recommends finding a natural moment, such as when the child asks about Mum's tummy or when you're shopping for baby things together. MedlinePlus also recommends that the child hear the news from the parents before everyone around them is talking about it. Q2: What if the older child regresses after the new baby arrives? AAP notes that regression is common — for example, accidents or wanting a bottle again. The recommendation is not to say "you're already grown up" but instead to praise them when they act like a big kid, and to set aside a daily period that belongs only to the older child. Q3: Should potty training happen before or after the new baby's birth? AAP recommends completing potty training or the transition to a bed before the baby is born if possible; if not, wait until after the baby is settled at home. Q4: Is there a custom picture book suitable for an older child? Yes. Tale With You's "big sibling" theme is [Child's name]'s Big-Sibling Practice: the child practices holding gently, speaking softly, folding tiny clothes, and saying "I'm a little nervous." # Mandarin Is Not My Native Language. Can I Still Help My Child Learn It? | Q&A Library | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

熊好學 · BearSay Mandarin BS10

# Mandarin Is Not My Native Language. Can I Still Help My Child Learn It?

Think BIG Q&A Library　·　November 9, 2026 　·　[中文版](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/non-native-parent-teach-mandarin/)

Short answer

Yes, you can help. The studies cited here point to how much the child hears and whether someone talks back and forth with them: bilingual children's performance in each language is related to the relative amount of input in it (Hoff et al., 2012); infants' sound discrimination needed live interaction and recordings had no effect (Kuhl et al., 2003); and children with more conversational turns with adults showed stronger language-region responses (Romeo et al., 2018). None of these studies measured parents' accents, so this page cannot say accent has no effect, and they do not address whether accent has long-term effects. When unsure of a pronunciation, check the Ministry of Education's official dictionary.

## 1. What the three studies say

Study Finding relevant to parents helping
Hoff et al. (2012) Bilingual toddlers' vocabulary and grammar in each language were related to the relative amount of input in it

Kuhl et al. (2003) 9-month-old infants kept Mandarin sound discrimination after live exposure; recordings had no effect

Romeo et al. (2018) Children aged 4 to 6 with more conversational turns with adults showed stronger language-region responses (correlational)

Sources: [Hoff et al., 2012](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0305000910000759); [Kuhl et al., 2003](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1532872100); [Romeo et al., 2018](https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797617742725).

## 2. What these studies do not say

They did not measure parents' accents.  None compared native with non-native parents, so no conclusion can be drawn that accent definitely matters, or definitely does not.

They guarantee nothing.  The findings are associations and laboratory results, not guarantees of learning outcomes.

They do not replace professional assessment.  If you are worried about your child's language development, ask a professional (see [two languages and speech delay](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/bilingual-children-language-delay/)).

## 3. What parents can do

1. Focus on amount and back-and-forth.  Pick a regular time each day and talk with your child in the Mandarin you can speak (see [practising speaking at home](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/practice-speaking-at-home/)).

2. Look up uncertain sounds.  The Ministry of Education's Revised Mandarin Dictionary gives pronunciations and meanings: [dict.revised.moe.edu.tw](https://dict.revised.moe.edu.tw/).

3. Bring in other Mandarin speakers.  Grandparents, friends, community groups and live online teachers all add chances for the child to hear Mandarin.

4. Treat media as a supplement.  Watch together and talk about it (see [can children learn Mandarin from videos](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/learn-language-from-video/)).

5. Learning together is fine.  Learning a word alongside your child, who sees an adult learning too, is a good model (this is a parenting practice, not a conclusion of the studies above).

Brand information | BearSay Mandarin

## BearSay Mandarin for parents learning alongside

Every day it teaches one Taiwan Mandarin word on Instagram ([@bearsaymandarin](https://www.instagram.com/bearsaymandarin/)), in Traditional characters with zhuyin and pinyin and multilingual subtitles, guided by five characters: BUBU, MIBO, HUBO, GUIBO and LANBO. The app is in development and has not been released. Release information will appear on the [BearSay Mandarin Q&A overview](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/bearsay/).

BearSay Mandarin's daily word comes with zhuyin, pinyin and multilingual subtitles, so parents can watch and learn with their children. BearSay Mandarin does not guarantee any learning result.

Source: the public Instagram account and this site's brand overview, updated 2026-11-09. Demo audio is AI-synthesized speech; BearSay Mandarin characters are AI-generated.

## Frequently asked questions

Q1: Can I help my child learn Mandarin if it is not my native language? Yes, you can help. The studies cited here point to how much the child hears and whether someone talks back and forth with them. None of them measured parents' accents, so this page cannot say accent has or has no effect. Q2: Does a non-standard parental accent affect children? None of the studies cited here directly measured parents' accents, so no conclusion can be drawn. They relate to amount of input and live interaction. Q3: What if I am unsure how to pronounce a word? Look it up in the Ministry of Education's Revised Mandarin Dictionary (dict.revised.moe.edu.tw). Q4: Should other people speak Mandarin with my child too? Yes. Grandparents, friends, community groups or live online teachers can increase how much Mandarin the child hears and the chances to interact.

- Kuhl, Tsao & Liu (2003). Foreign-language experience in infancy. PNAS, 100(15), 9096–9101: [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1532872100)

- Romeo et al. (2018). Beyond the 30-million-word gap. Psychological Science, 29(5), 700–710: [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797617742725)

# Can a Local LLM Work Offline, and How Do You Update Models and Software in an Air-Gapped Environment?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-19
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/offline-local-llm-updates/)

The short answer

Yes. After a model is downloaded to the machine, answering questions needs no network. Truly offline operation takes three things: turning off cloud features (Ollama supports OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 ), not applying automatic updates directly (Ollama on macOS and Windows downloads updates automatically), and changing updates to "download, verify, and test on a connected machine, then move into the offline environment and install".

## 1. What needs a network

Using Ollama as the example (checked against official documentation on 2026-10-19):

Action
Network needed?
Notes
Answering with a downloaded model
No
Ollama states that when you run locally, it does not see your prompts or data

Downloading models (ollama pull )
Yes
Ollama FAQ: Ollama pulls models from the internet and may require a proxy

Software updates
Yes
macOS and Windows download updates automatically, applied via "Restart to update"; on Linux, rerun the install script

Cloud models and web search
Yes
Unavailable once cloud features are disabled

Other tools an AI Agent uses (web search, email, LINE) need a network by nature. For an offline environment, decide first whether to remove them or allow them only to specific destinations.

## 2. Offline settings checklist

- Turn off cloud features.  Set OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 , or set disable_ollama_cloud  in ~/.ollama/server.json . After a restart, the log shows Ollama cloud disabled: true .

- Pin the version; do not apply auto-updates directly.  Record the current version. Leave "Restart to update" alone until an update has been tested.

- Serve only on the machine or the internal network.  Ollama binds to 127.0.0.1  port 11434 by default. To let other internal devices connect, open access to specific devices through a firewall.

- Set the model location.  Use OLLAMA_MODELS  to set the model directory for easier backup, transfer, and control.

- Test with the network actually cut.  With outbound connections blocked at the firewall, confirm Q&A still works and check connection logs for any unexpected outbound traffic.

## 3. Five steps for offline updates

- Download on a connected test machine.  Get the new software and model files on a separate test machine.

- Verify source and hashes.  OWASP's supply chain guidance: use only models from verifiable sources and check integrity with signing and file hashes.

- Run the same test questions.  After a model or version change, rerun the company's fixed test set to confirm answer quality has not regressed (see "Is a local LLM smart enough?").

- Move it in on approved media.  Models can be imported as GGUF: create a Modelfile  with FROM /path/to/file.gguf , then run ollama create model-name . Ollama's documentation notes it does not quantize GGUF files on import, so prepare the quantized file in advance.

- Record versions and keep the old one.  Note versions, dates, and test results before and after; keep the previous version so you can roll back.

## FAQ

Q1: Can Ollama run completely offline? Yes. Once a model is downloaded, answering needs no network. To keep it from reaching the cloud, set `OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1` or `disable_ollama_cloud` in server.json; the trade-off is losing cloud models and web search. Q2: How do you install a new model without internet? Download the GGUF model file on a connected machine and check its hash, move it to the offline machine, create a Modelfile with `FROM /path/to/file.gguf`, and run `ollama create`. Q3: Does Ollama update itself? Per the official FAQ, the macOS and Windows versions download updates automatically and apply them when you choose "Restart to update"; on Linux you rerun the install script. For production, pin the version and update only after testing. Q4: How do you confirm a local model makes no outbound connections? Run a real Q&A test with outbound connections blocked at the firewall, and check connection logs for any unexpected outbound traffic.

# On-Premises, Private Cloud, or Public Cloud: Where Does AI Data Actually Go? | Q&A Library | Think BIG

# On-Premises, Private Cloud, or Public Cloud: Where Does AI Data Actually Go?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-11-08
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/on-prem-private-public-cloud/)

The short answer

On-premises usually describes deployment on company-designated equipment at its site. Private and public cloud describe cloud infrastructure use. NIST allows a private cloud to exist on or off premises, so the label alone does not locate the data. Check models, documents, indexes, logs, backups, and integrations separately.

## 1. Location and deployment model are separate dimensions

NIST SP 800-145 (2011) defines private cloud for a single organization and allows operation by the organization or a third party, on or off premises. Public cloud is open for public use and exists at the provider’s premises. An on-premises system may also be a private cloud.

Term
Main meaning
What it does not establish
On-premises
Deployment on designated equipment at the company site
Offline operation or no outbound traffic

Private cloud
Cloud infrastructure for one organization
A company-site or Taiwan location

Public cloud
Cloud infrastructure open for public use
Public access to company documents

A company-owned cloud account or server alone does not establish a NIST private cloud. Ask what is dedicated: an account, network, compute resources, or physical equipment.

## 2. Trace data through the workflow

Ollama’s FAQ distinguishes local processing from cloud-model use and documents a way to disable cloud features. Feature selection can change data flows even when the application stays on the same machine.

We suggest mapping employee input, application, retrieval, model processing, and output, then adding logs, monitoring, and backups. For each connection, record location, recipient service, fields transmitted, retention, and account owner.

A local interface and local files can still send passages to a remote model. Cloud infrastructure, conversely, does not make documents public. Access controls, storage regions, and terms need separate review. This is a data-flow assessment rather than a ranking of deployment options.

## 3. Ask four questions before selecting an option

Identify permitted data destinations, maintenance and incident owners, work that must survive an outage, and handover or deletion procedures. Turn each answer into a setting, document, or acceptance check.

An organization may use approved cloud services for some work and assess local processing for more restricted material. This is a planning suggestion subject to company rules and operational capacity. Record locations, access, and external services for either option.

Brand information | Think BIG

## Deployment and external connections at Think BIG

Think BIG helps companies deploy AI Agents in their own environments. Running on company hardware does not keep every connection local: cloud models, messaging platforms, and other external services can still receive requests.

- Map data flows first : Before deployment, identify data sources, processing locations, output recipients, logs, and backups. Assess deployment location and external connections separately.

- Set permissions for the task : Define read and write access using least privilege. A designated person decides on external sending, spending, and changes to production systems.

See [Trust](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/) and [Local AI and data sovereignty](https://thinkbigtw.com/guides/local-ai-data/).

The actual scope of Think BIG’s services follows what both parties confirm.

## FAQ

Q1: Is private cloud always in the company’s data center? No. NIST SP 800-145 (2011) allows on- or off-premises deployment. Q2: Does public cloud make data public? No. Infrastructure availability and document access are separate questions. Q3: Does a company-owned cloud account mean private cloud? Account ownership alone is insufficient; examine the infrastructure and service architecture. Q4: Does local installation still need a data-flow map? Yes. Check external models, messaging, logs, and backups individually.

# Open Model Commercial Use: 4 License Checks | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

# Can Open Models Be Used Commercially? Four License Checks Before a Company Adopts One

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-19
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/open-model-license-checklist/)

The short answer

Not always. It depends on the license of the exact version you download, not on the model's reputation or the word "open". Before adopting one, check four things: whether the license allows commercial use, whether there is a user-count or revenue threshold, whether there is an acceptable use policy (a list of prohibited uses), and what conditions apply to derivative models and redistribution. Versions within the same model family can carry different licenses.

## 1. "Open" does not mean "anything goes"

In everyday use, "open-source model" usually means a model whose weights you can download and run on your own hardware; "open-weight" is the more precise term. Being downloadable does not mean there are no conditions. The conditions are in the license file that comes with each model.

Licenses fall roughly into two groups:

- General permissive open-source licenses , such as the Apache License 2.0: they grant royalty-free rights to reproduce, prepare derivative works, and distribute. Redistribution requires including a copy of the license, marking modified files as changed, and retaining existing copyright and license notices.

- Licenses or terms written by the model provider : these may add user-scale thresholds, prohibited uses, attribution rules, or naming rules for derivative models.

So the answer to "can we use it commercially?" always comes from the official license text for that version.

## 2. Four checks before adoption

Check
What to look for
Why it matters
1. Commercial use allowed
Whether the grant is restricted to research or non-commercial use
Some models allow only research or personal use

2. User-count or revenue threshold
Above what number of users or revenue a separate license is required
Most small and mid-sized companies will not reach it, but confirm whether it exists and where it sits

3. Acceptable use policy
The prohibited-use list, and whether it is a condition of the license
Breaching a prohibited use can mean breaching the license

4. Derivative models and redistribution
How fine-tuned models must be named, whether attribution is required, what must accompany distribution
Installing a model in a system delivered to a customer may count as redistribution

Read each model's official license page yourself: find the license file (usually LICENSE) on the model's official download page or repository and match it to the version number you actually downloaded.

## 3. Record licenses in the component inventory

OWASP's supply chain guidance for LLM applications (LLM03:2025) recommends inventorying all license types involved with a bill of materials (BOM) and keeping an up-to-date software bill of materials (SBOM). In practice, for each system you should be able to look up:

- Which model, which version, and where it was downloaded from.

- The license name for that version and a copy of the license file.

- The licenses of the tools and packages that run the model, recorded separately from the model license.

- The result of the four checks, with who confirmed it and when.

When a model is updated, read the new version's license again. Licensing involves legal judgment; before commercial use, have legal counsel confirm against your actual use.

## FAQ

Q1: Can all open-source models be used commercially for free? Not always. Being able to download the weights does not mean there are no conditions. Check the license of the exact version: some allow only research use, and some have user-scale thresholds or prohibited-use lists. Q2: How do you confirm whether a model can be used commercially? Find the license file on the model's official download page or repository, match it to the version you downloaded, and check four points: commercial use, user-count or revenue thresholds, acceptable use policy, and derivative and redistribution conditions. Q3: Can a fine-tuned model be sold or delivered to customers? It depends on the original license's terms for derivative models and redistribution, such as naming rules, attribution requirements, and documents that must accompany distribution. Installing a model in a system delivered to a customer may count as redistribution. Q4: How should a company manage the model licenses it uses? Record model, version, download source, license file, and check results in the component inventory (SBOM), record tool and package licenses separately, and recheck when models are updated. Have legal counsel confirm before commercial use.

Sources (checked 2026-10-19)

- Apache License, Version 2.0 (Section 2 grant, Section 4 redistribution conditions): [www.apache.org](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0)

- OWASP, LLM03:2025 Supply Chain (license inventory via BOM, SBOM, verifiable sources): [genai.owasp.org](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm032025-supply-chain/)

TB25

# Open Weights or Open Source: What Is the Difference for Enterprise AI?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-11-07
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/open-weights-vs-open-source/)

The short answer

“Open weights” generally describes access to learned model parameters. “Open source” also concerns the materials needed for modification and the freedom to use, study, change, and share them. Downloadable files alone do not establish open-source status or suitability for a company’s intended use. Check the actual release and its license.

## 1. Weights are one part of a model

OSI’s Open Source AI Definition 1.0 describes weights as learned parameters and identifies data information, code, and parameters as elements needed for modification. It also sets out four freedoms. A download link alone does not establish compliance.

This is OSI’s definition, not Taiwan legislation or a legal determination about a particular model. Here, “open weights” describes availability rather than a uniform license. State which files are available and which terms apply instead of using one label for an entire system.

## 2. Read availability claims separately

Claim
What it indicates
What remains to check
Downloadable weights
Access to parameter files
Uses, modifications, and redistribution

Public code
Visibility of some code
License and covered files

Open-source compliance
A claim against a definition
Actual terms and release materials

OSI’s software definition covers more than source visibility, including redistribution, derived works, and freedom across fields of endeavor. Its AI definition calls for sufficient training-data information; this should not be reduced to a claim that all raw training data must be public.

For rebuilding, modification, or handover, list the materials the company needs and compare them with the release.

## 3. Keep versions and licenses traceable

Hugging Face documents license metadata in model cards and license text for custom terms. These labels help locate the terms; they do not remove the need to read them.

We suggest recording the publisher, version, license URL, and intended use separately for weights, inference code, tokenizers, plugins, and data sources. Ask counsel or the rights holder about unclear terms before adoption. This is general information, not legal advice.

Open weights also do not determine data residency. Execution locations, cloud connections, and log access require separate deployment and security review.

Brand information | Think BIG

## Third-party component and version review at Think BIG

Think BIG helps companies deploy AI Agents in their own environments. Running on company hardware does not keep every connection local: cloud models, messaging platforms, and other external services can still receive requests.

- Review third-party components : Third-party packages are reviewed for source and licensing, pinned, and kept off automatic updates. Keys are stored in access-protected configuration files and are not shared in chat.

- Verify work with evidence : Completion criteria require corresponding change records and verification results, with maintenance and handover responsibilities defined.

See [Trust](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/) and [Local AI and data sovereignty](https://thinkbigtw.com/guides/local-ai-data/).

The actual scope of Think BIG’s services follows what both parties confirm.

## FAQ

Q1: Is every downloadable model open source? No. Check the relevant definition, actual license, and release materials. Q2: Is OSI’s definition law? No. This article explains its terminology without making a legal determination about a license. Q3: Must all raw training data be public? OSI 1.0 requires sufficient data information; that is not the same as publishing every raw training item. Q4: Can one model license cover every component? Record terms separately for the model, code, plugins, and other materials rather than assuming they match.

- OSI, The Open Source Definition: [opensource.org](https://opensource.org/osd)

- Hugging Face, Licenses: [huggingface.co](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/repositories-licenses)

# What Official Resources Can Overseas Children Use to Learn Mandarin at Home?

Think BIG Q&A Library　·　November 9, 2026 　·　[中文版](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/overseas-kids-learn-mandarin-resources/)

Short answer

Overseas families can start with Huayuworld (全球華文網), run by Taiwan's Overseas Community Affairs Council. Its series Let's Learn Mandarin (For Children) is built on second-language teaching concepts, with 12 units per volume containing dialogues, vocabulary lists, sentence-pattern practice, rhymes and games. Phonetic marks are zhuyin and pinyin, with Simplified characters noted alongside, and it suits primary to junior-high ages. The site also has a games section and a Traditional-character resource section. Whether content is free or needs registration follows the site's own notices.

## 1. What Huayuworld offers

Section Content
E-books: Let's Learn Mandarin (For Children) Based on second-language teaching concepts, 12 units per volume with dialogues, vocabulary lists, sentence-pattern practice, rhymes and games; zhuyin and pinyin, with Simplified characters noted; suits primary to junior-high ages

Teaching resources: Learning Mandarin through games Includes digital games for the series, a Moedict word-block game and the "Qunxiong Gesentence" board game

Teaching resources: Traditional characters Collects resources for teaching Traditional characters

Sources: [Let's Learn Mandarin (For Children)](https://www.huayuworld.org/Ebook/LearnMandarinChildren), [games section](https://www.huayuworld.org/MandarinResourcesDetail/MandarinResourcesDetail/Index/9), [Huayuworld home page](https://www.huayuworld.org/). The site has login and registration; which content needs a login and whether any is charged follows the site's own notices.

## 2. Using them at home

Short and regular.  Rather than finishing a volume in one sitting, take a small slice each day (see [daily practice time](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/daily-practice-spaced-review/)).

People still need to speak Mandarin.  A child's performance in each language is related to how much input there is in that language (see [two languages and speech delay](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/bilingual-children-language-delay/)). Materials give content, but speaking chances come from family, friends and community.

Start with one phonetic system.  The series marks both zhuyin and pinyin, so the child can begin with the one that feels familiar (see [zhuyin or pinyin first](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/zhuyin-or-pinyin-for-kids/)).

Look up sounds in the official dictionary.  The Ministry of Education's Revised Mandarin Dictionary gives pronunciations and meanings: [dict.revised.moe.edu.tw](https://dict.revised.moe.edu.tw/).

## 3. Things to note

The series notes Simplified characters. If a family wants the child to meet mainly Traditional characters, the Traditional-character section can be used alongside. Try a sample first to see whether it suits your child; this site does not rank teaching materials.

Brand information | BearSay Mandarin

The app is in development and has not been released. Release information will appear on the [BearSay Mandarin Q&A overview](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/bearsay/).

BearSay Mandarin's daily word uses Traditional characters, zhuyin and pinyin with multilingual subtitles, and can be found on Instagram by families overseas. It can be used alongside official materials but does not replace them, and does not guarantee any learning result.

Source: the public Instagram account and this site's brand overview, updated 2026-11-09. Demo audio is AI-synthesized speech; BearSay Mandarin characters are AI-generated.
